Sean Hannity: Stephen A. Smith, our friend, was back at the White House today, sparking speculation that he could be President Trump's new press secretary. I can promise you, that's not going to happen. Anyway, Stephen A. addressed that with reporters. Here's what he said.

Reporter: What about the press secretary role? Did you discuss that?

Stephen A. Smith: No. No, not at all.

Reporter: Did he offer you it?

Stephen A. Smith: No way in hell. No way in hell.

Sean Hannity: Anyway, so what was Stephen A. doing at the White House? He was there to interview President Trump for his podcast. They spoke for nearly an hour, a wide range of topics, including how the president does plan to work with Democrats over the next two years. Take a look.

Stephen A. Smith: What about you over your last two years in office? What are you going to do dealing with the Democrats? Are you, is there anything that you change? Is there anything that you're going to do differently? Are you willing to work with them? I know you said you have. You're willing to.

Donald Trump: So I'm going to be, I'm going to be vetoing a lot of things that they're going to send me initially that are bad for the country. And I think eventually they're going to call in. They're going to say, let's make a deal and we'll be able to make deals on, on healthcare, on drug prices.

Sean Hannity: Here now is the man himself, ESPN hosts, our friend, Stephen A. Smith. All right. You got to admit the question about you being the press secretary. That was pretty darn funny.

Stephen A. Smith: That was great. That was, that was absolutely hilarious. Evidently, they don't know about the life that I live and the kind of affluence that ESPN and Disney have blessed me with. It ain't taking that day. I wouldn't take that pay cut for almost anything but the presidency. And even then, I mean, you know, you got to, you got to give it up before you campaign. That's why that's not going to happen. It would take the presidency, me winning the presidency in order for me to even consider giving up what I have. That ain't happening.

Sean Hannity: All right, now the president and I did talk about you. He did ask me a lot of questions going into this interview. Asked my thoughts about him doing the interview with you. I gave it to him. Of course, I said, we're, we're longtime friends. I'd absolutely do it. He promised you that. Why don't you take us inside, talk. What did you all talk about?

Stephen A. Smith: Well, the first order of business is to let your audience know you're absolutely right. I don't think the interview would have happened without you. So I appreciate that, no doubt. You know, he promised me we were going to sit down and sure enough when we sat down, I think, you know, obviously the war in Iran, the tariffs have obviously had a profound effect on our, on our economy, on our society as a whole, in terms of how everybody is looking at things from an affordability perspective. I definitely challenged him on that. He gave a lot of pushback on that. Of course, we talked about the devastating losses in the midterms and how the GOP essentially got slaughtered, not to the degree of the 63 seats that Obama lost in 2010, or the inordinate amount of seats that Clinton lost in 1994, but it was still a lot, over 40 seats in the House, obviously significant seats in the Senate, about five governorships throughout the country. And I can't ignore what happened with Kansas that turned blue for the first time since 1932. So I brought all of that up and I asked him, is he willing to point the finger at himself? And he was dogged. He was, he was, no way, he was, he was immovable in that regard. He said, I wasn't on the ballot. I said, that makes absolutely no sense, Mr. President. You said, put you on a ballot. That's what you told the American people to do. He said, well, they didn't do it. I said, well, what if they did do it? And that was the reason you lost. He refused to accept that. His attitude is that the candidates were not that great. If it were him that was running, this would not have happened. That's his mentality. He doesn't believe they put him on a ballot. And to me, I, I'm not, I don't think that he's lying. I think that he is somebody that is convinced his way is, is what it is. I just don't agree with them. I think that the American people made a statement against what they were seeing from him in terms of him not having his eye on the ball and coming across as a bit detached in their eyes. They don't believe him to be the Donald Trump that he once was. I basically broached all of these subjects with him, but he had an answer for everything, which is predictable. And, you know, he, he was just very rigid and immovable in his thinking that it was blown by the people who lost and that the candidates on the Republican side simply were not good enough. It was not about him. I don't disagree. I don't agree with that, but nevertheless, I give him credit. I asked a question and he answered it. He didn't run from anything that I do that with everybody in fairness. And I've been on your podcast. It's not an interview that Joe Biden would ever do, or would be capable of doing.

Sean Hannity: You have been very outspoken. But it's not just him. It's not just, it's not just Biden. There's a whole bunch of Democrats that haven't done it. Just to be clear.

Stephen A. Smith: I've invited Barack Obama on my, on my show. I've invited Michelle Obama on my show, AOC, Jasmine Crockett, Bernie Sanders, Hakeem Jeffries has come on. That, that's absolutely it. Wes Moore has come on, Senator Cory Booker has come on along with a few other Democrats.

Sean Hannity: I want to ask you one more question, but not those names that you've been very outspoken about the radicals within the democratic party and how dangerous you think their policies are. Does that come up? And now that the radicals have won, what are your thoughts?

Stephen A. Smith: I didn't need to bring that up because to be honest with you, I'm aligned with most people, moderates and folks on the right in this country in terms of thinking about how dangerous that is. I'm not, I'm a moderate. I'm not a progressive leftist, and I don't believe that's good for the United States of America. And I'm not apologizing for that to a damn soul. I think it would be disastrous if the country fell into that kind of leadership personally. That's just how I feel about it. I've been very honest about it, very unapologetic. And I'm just as immovable as the president or anybody else is that, that believes such things. Cause I think that would be bad for the country. We did not need to get into that. No question about it, but I definitely think that right now the Democrats have a challenge on their hands because clearly there's a lot of people out there that viewed the Democratic party as a divided party. Now they will tell you they're a very big tent and there's room for everybody. But I think that the progressive left has shown you there isn't room for everybody because if you're not willing to capitulate to their desires, their wishes and their ideological beliefs 100% and they got a problem with you, you can agree with 97, 98% of what they do. Not that I don't, not that I do because I don't, but you can agree with 98%. They'll hold the 2% against you as if you're a sworn enemy, at least that's how their behavior has come across. And I don't think that's something that's good for the country. I think when they watch this podcast, they should go back and watch the one we did recently because I thought it was a lot of fun.

Sean Hannity: Stephen A., thank you as always for being on the show. We appreciate it. All right. Thanks for watching. Check out my new podcast, hanging out with me, Sean Hannity, the big interviews, the debates you won't get anywhere else. Like and subscribe for new episodes every Tuesday and Thursday.

The inner life can keep opening throughout a lifetime.

Charlotte Joko Beck describes Zen practice as a continuing study of the mind and of the way we live. Sitting brings attention to the busy movement of thought, while the larger practice includes work, relationships, and everyday activity.

The opening she describes has consequences for compassion. As understanding deepens, she says, it becomes something we express in how we meet other people. This gives spiritual practice an ongoing, relational character. Each stage of life can offer further room for clarity and care, and the ordinary circumstances of the day remain part of that unfolding study.

Three years is not a short time. In the life of a nation, three years is enough for a seed to become a harvest.

In May 2023, President Bola Tinubu inherited a soft economy. Fuel at about N195, Dollar at about N750, a bag of rice at about N30,000. He asked Nigerians for patience and promised Renewed Hope.

Three years later, the market has given its verdict! Fuel at over N1,400, Dollar at over N1,600, a bag of rice at over N100,000.

In three years, reform has felt like punishment. Taxation without production. Policy without empathy. Statistics that grow on paper while pockets grow empty.

Nigerians are not impatient. Nigerians have simply checked their pockets. And the pockets are empty.

Contrast this with Atiku Abubakar's first three years as Vice President, 1999-2002.

Nigeria in 1999 had no GSM, dead public enterprises, and a pariah economy. Atiku, as Chairman of the National Council on Privatization, did not announce pain. He engineered progress.

He liberalized telecommunications and gave Nigeria its first 20 million mobile lines. He championed the privatization that revived dead sectors. He assembled and empowered the economic management team that restored investor confidence and paved the way for debt relief.

In three years, Atiku did not tell Nigerians to endure hardship. He created the private economy that allowed Nigerians to escape hardship.

That is the difference between a reformer and a ruler.

One builds institutions. The other offers excuses.

One creates prosperity. The other creates poverty.

Nigeria does not need more patience. Nigeria needs a plan that works.

Atiku Is Coming.
It's Atiku O’clock. 

— Shafiu Balarabe.

DEVOTIONAL:  Jewels from Junk

“…I know what I’m doing. I have it all planned out—plans to take care of you, not abandon you, plans to give you the future you hope for.” Jeremiah 29:11 (The Message)

‘You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.’ Song of Solomon 4:7

In her poem ‘What to do with bits of string’, poet Luci Shaw writes, “Women in Africa roll old magazines into beads, varnishing them for sale in other worlds, jewels from junk.” When I read those words, I recalled the roadside stand in an African country where a young girl sat selling ornaments made by her mother and aunt. Earrings, shiny red metal cut into small circles with the Coca Cola  logo clearly visible. Bracelets made from newsprint rolled tightly into cylinders only a quarter inch in diameter. Brooches crafted from fallen bits of woods, rubbed shiny and with a safety pin glued to the back.

I wear bits of jewellery like these and love to tell stories of their creation when people offer their compliments. Some women have even asked how they can learn to make such baubles to earn extra spending money although many grow silent and somewhat pensive when I explain that the mere pennies I paid will buy rice for a family’s supper that evening.

Too often we see ourselves only as ordinary junk. Perhaps we have not grown up with affirmation or, much worse, we have been abused and heard shouts that we are nothing but junk. We compare ourselves to those who possess more, who have attained more, who appear more beautiful or handsome. We see ourselves as mere bottle caps, bit of discarded wood or newsprint.

Then God breaks in with the message He declared at creation:  “This is VERY good!” And as He works in our lives to re-create us after sin’s damaging work, He says: “I know what I’m doing…You are altogether beautiful…I have plans to take care of you…” In a very real sense, God is taking the raw material of our lives, polishing us, shaping us into not mere baubles, but into valuable gems to tell the world that we are jewels, not junk.

Lord, is it unseemly, prideful to call myself a jewel? Or is a statement that gives you all the glory for loving me so much? Help me see myself—and others—as beautiful because of your great love.
Spend time today thanking God specifically for the way He has created you. Then look for someone who needs an affirming word that they, too, have been created as precious jewels.

By Marilyn Ehle Used by Permission

text:
AN View / Life in Motion / Policy, Incentives & Human Agency

A POLICY DOES NOT ACT ON ITS OWN. PEOPLE GIVE IT FORCE.

Research published in Nature on November 11 examines a crucial part of China's one-child policy that helps explain why the country's fertility rate fell so sharply during the 1990s, more than a decade after the policy was introduced. 

Researchers from Stanford University and Renmin University of China found that the introduction of a performance rule known as the One-Vote Veto tied local officials' career advancement directly to meeting birth-control targets. Their analysis estimates that this enforcement mechanism accounted for nearly half of China's fertility decline during the 1990s.

The findings reveal how the personal incentives of people responsible for implementing a policy can shape its consequences on a much larger scale. The researchers also documented changes in contraceptive use, including increased use of methods recommended by local officials, and a rise in induced abortions in later years.

 The study does not suggest that bureaucratic incentives were the only cause of declining fertility; economic development and wider social changes also mattered. It does, however, offer a closer look at how institutional targets can enter people's most personal decisions.

An Observation from AN View

Between a policy and its consequences are people who interpret, enforce and experience it. Understanding social change means paying attention to all three, not only to the intentions written into a rule.

🔬 DEEP DIVE: Finger Dislocations Are Clustering Across Pro Sports — Here's What the Biology Actually Means for NFL Players

Finger dislocation (proximal interphalangeal joint, most common presentation) | Severity: MODERATE

Finger dislocations have surfaced across multiple rosters in the current reporting window — Colton Hood of the New York Giants, Justin Herbert of the Los Angeles Chargers, Lauri Markkanen of the Utah Jazz, and Bennedict Mathurin of the New Orleans Pelicans have all been affected. While finger dislocations are often waved off as minor nuisances, the clinical reality is significantly more layered, particularly at skill positions in the NFL where hand function is a core performance requirement. This deep-dive focuses on what finger dislocations actually involve biologically, how they're graded, and what the evidence says about return to play — with the NFL context front and center.

A finger dislocation occurs when the bones of a digit are forcibly displaced from their normal articular alignment. The most commonly involved joint in sports is the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint — the middle knuckle — though metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint dislocations also occur. The tissue disrupted is ligamentous (the collateral ligaments and volar plate, a dense fibrocartilaginous structure on the palm side of the joint that resists hyperextension), placing these injuries squarely in the ligament category on the tissue axis. Anatomically, the injury is classified as an upper extremity event. In terms of structural severity, finger dislocations span a wide spectrum: a simple dorsal PIP dislocation with an intact volar plate after reduction is functionally a Grade 2 ligamentous injury, while a fracture-dislocation — where the volar plate avulses a bony fragment or the joint surface is compromised — escalates to Grade 3 with surgical implications. For the cases in this window, grades are inferred from available reporting rather than confirmed by imaging disclosure.

The mechanism varies by sport but follows a consistent theme: an axial load or hyperextension force applied to the fingertip while the joint is partially flexed. In football, this happens constantly — a wide receiver's finger catching on a defender's jersey during a route, a lineman's hand getting caught in a pile, a quarterback's throwing hand impacting a helmet on a follow-through. Justin Herbert, as the Chargers' franchise quarterback, represents the highest-stakes version of this injury in the NFL context. Even a seemingly minor PIP dislocation on the throwing hand can alter grip mechanics, release point, and ball spin — functional consequences that don't show up on an X-ray but absolutely show up on the field. Herbert's grade is inferred from practice participation language, not confirmed imaging disclosure. Colton Hood, a Giants tight end, faces a different demand profile — blocking and contested-catch mechanics both load the fingers significantly, and even a buddy-taped digit changes how a tight end handles a jam route or absorbs a defensive back's hands.

The anatomy here matters. The volar plate is the primary stabilizer against PIP hyperextension, and it is the structure most commonly disrupted in dorsal dislocations. When it tears partially (Grade 2), the joint retains meaningful stability and conservative management — reduction, splinting in slight flexion, and progressive buddy taping — is appropriate. When the volar plate avulses a bony fragment from the base of the middle phalanx (the classic "volar plate avulsion fracture"), the decision tree becomes surgical if the fragment is large enough to compromise joint congruence or if the joint remains unstable after reduction. The collateral ligaments, which prevent lateral deviation of the finger, are frequently injured simultaneously and add another layer of instability to assess. This is why the initial post-reduction X-ray is so critical — the difference between a stable simple dislocation and an unstable fracture-dislocation is a clinical and radiographic determination, not a sideline one.

Treatment protocols follow a well-established algorithm. For stable reductions without significant fracture component, early controlled motion is now preferred over prolonged rigid immobilization — the literature consistently shows that early motion reduces stiffness, maintains cartilage health, and shortens functional recovery time without compromising stability. Buddy taping to the adjacent finger provides lateral support while allowing flexion-extension, and most athletes at the NFL level can return to participation quickly with this approach. The practical reality in professional football is that most simple PIP dislocations are reduced on the sideline, buddy-taped, and the player returns to the same game — which is why they're often minimized in reporting. The nuanced point is that "returned to game" is not the same as "fully healed." The volar plate and collateral ligaments that were disrupted require six to eight weeks of biological remodeling even when the player is functionally active, and re-dislocation risk during that window is real.

Fracture-dislocations and volar dislocations — which are less common but clinically more serious — tell a different story entirely. Volar PIP dislocations can trap the central slip of the extensor tendon between the joint surfaces, making closed reduction impossible and potentially leading to boutonnière deformity if the central slip is not repaired. Any PIP dislocation that cannot be reduced on the sideline, any that remains unstable after reduction, and any with a significant fracture component should be evaluated for surgical fixation. Post-surgical timelines for PIP fracture-dislocations are measured in months, not days — typically 8 to 16 weeks depending on the fixation construct and the demands of the position. For a quarterback like Herbert, surgical intervention on the throwing hand would trigger a full timeline reset anchored to that procedure date, not the original dislocation date.

The NBA cases — Markkanen and Mathurin — provide useful sport comparison context. Basketball generates similar finger dislocation mechanisms (ball impact, reaching for a rebound, a ball handler's finger catching a defender's hand), and the demand on hand function for a shooting guard or a stretch forward is analogous in many ways to a quarterback. Markkanen's shooting mechanics and Mathurin's ball-handling would both be sensitive to even subtle PIP instability. The cross-sport clustering of this injury type in a single reporting window is likely coincidental — finger dislocations are among the most common athletic hand injuries year-round — but it offers a useful reminder that the injury is rarely as simple as it looks from the stands.

The evidence base for finger dislocation RTP is classified as T2 — moderate confidence. There are no large randomized controlled trials governing return-to-play timelines for PIP dislocations specifically in professional athletes, but observational literature and established hand surgery protocols provide reasonably consistent guidance. For simple, stable dislocations managed conservatively, functional return (with buddy taping and protective equipment) typically occurs within one to four weeks. Full biological healing of the volar plate and collateral ligaments — the kind of healing that fully restores joint stability without protective equipment — takes six to eight weeks at minimum. For fracture-dislocations requiring surgical fixation, the range extends to three to four months. The clinical take is straightforward: finger dislocations sit in a wide severity spectrum, the initial sideline presentation is frequently misleading about true structural damage, and position-specific hand demands — particularly for quarterbacks and pass-catchers — mean that even "minor" dislocations deserve more clinical scrutiny than they typically receive in sports media coverage.

text:
Far-left Rep Pramila Jayapal schooled on First Amendment by X's Community Notes | Ari Hoffman, The Post Millennial

Rep. Pramila Jayapal apparently needs a refresher on the First Amendment. Freedom of speech does not guarantee a rapper that he can book the arena of his choice, but she doesn’t know that.

The Washington Democrat invoked free speech while pressuring Climate Pledge Arena to host Macklemore’s “Free Palestine” benefit tour.

“Freedom of Speech is a paramount right in this country. It is wrong that Seattle’s own Climate Pledge Arena is reportedly blocking Macklemore’s performance. I call on Climate Pledge to make every effort to ensure Macklemore is able to perform in his own hometown arena,” Jayapal wrote.

“Seattle is better than this.”

Her post received a Community Note explaining the distinction a member of Congress should understand: The First Amendment protects against government restrictions on speech. It does not require private venues to book performers.

The Supreme Court has explained that private entities generally are not bound by the First Amendment’s restrictions on government. Hosting someone else’s speech does not automatically turn a private operator into a government actor.

Macklemore can express his views. That does not give him a constitutional entitlement to someone else’s stage. Under Jayapal’s logic, a radio host could demand to broadcast their radio show from her home.

Macklemore claimed nine American arenas declined his tour, including Climate Pledge Arena, home to the Seattle Kraken, which the arena owner partly owns. MSG Entertainment offered a blunt explanation: “We have some of the busiest venues in the world with extremely limited availability and he’s not an arena-level act.”

Jayapal’s comments also overlook the controversy surrounding the tour’s beneficiaries.

The tour raises money for organizations facing government scrutiny or allegations of supporting Hamas and other designated terrorist groups.

Among the beneficiaries is UNRWA USA, which raises money for the UN agency. 101 of their current and former employees were referred by USAID’s inspector general for possible suspension or debarment over alleged participation in October 7 or affiliation with Hamas’ military wing. Another beneficiary, HEAL Palestine, faced a South Carolina attorney general inquiry into nonprofits potentially supporting Hamas.

The ADL documented Middle East Children’s Alliance raising $70,000 for a Viva Palestina convoy whose participants met Hamas leaders. NGO Monitor alleged that Taawon partnered with organizations linked to the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine. Palestinian Youth Movement, also a beneficiary, co-hosted a demonstration the day after October 7 where speakers praised Hamas’ attack.

At his October 30 London concert, Macklemore also wore a “Free Marwan” shirt and brought Marwan Barghouti’s son onstage. Barghouti is serving five life sentences for his role in attacks that killed five people, including a Greek monk.

Jayapal’s Macklemore post was the second time in two days that her statements drew a Community Note. The other appeared on a KOMO News post quoting her vow to “take our state back” and plan to overturn voter-approved initiatives.

Take it back from whom?

Democrats had just secured a supermajority in Washington’s state House while retaining control of the Senate. Voters rejected four moderate state Supreme Court candidates and two conservative-backed initiatives but approved I-638, designed to keep boys out of girls’ sports.

The Community Note made it clear to the congresswoman: Democrats already control every level of Washington’s government.

The effort to overturn I-638 is already underway. The ACLU, Legal Voice and Pacifica Law Group are challenging the measure on behalf of plaintiffs including the Washington Education Association teachers’ union and TransFamilies, seeking to block it before its December 3 effective date.

One Community Note explained who governs her state. The next explained the limits of the constitutional protection she invoked. Both supplied information a sitting congresswoman should already know.

Arizona Elementary Students Didn’t Slow Down At 100-Degree Recess | StudyFinds

In A Nutshell

- Phoenix-area fourth and fifth graders reported more hard recess play on days above 100 degrees than on days below 95.

- Reported activity held steady for six weeks, even as kids said they felt hot.

- Kids rated their heat after recess, so exertion may explain the link, and cause is unproven.

- Researchers say schools should rely on shade, water, and schedule changes.

---

Fourth and fifth graders in the Phoenix area did not back off at recess when temperatures climbed past 100 degrees. In surveys filled out right after recess, reports of hard, breathless play rose from 12.5% of responses on days below 95 degrees to 36.4% on days above 100. Rising heat did not slow these kids down, a result that raises a safety question for schools in hot regions.

In the study, published in PLOS Global Public Health, researchers collected data during the first six weeks of the 2024-2025 school year. That stretch overlapped with Phoenix’s hottest September and hottest year at the time, plus its longest run of days at or above 100 degrees on record. Recess is often the main chance for free play during the school day, and in earlier research on 91-to-109-degree days, 60% of observed recess periods at Arizona elementary schools were still held outdoors.

One caution comes first. Students rated how hot they felt only after recess ended, so running hard may have made them feel hotter, rather than heat pushing them to play harder. Researchers stress that the results show a link, not a cause. A kid who just sprinted around the yard will naturally rate the heat higher, whether or not the heat made that child run.

Harder Recess Play Rose With Heat in Phoenix Schools

Schools were randomly selected from a list of 57 Phoenix-area schools that had earlier said heat affected their recess. Principals at five schools agreed to join, and four made the final analysis. On Tuesdays and Thursdays from August 1 through September 11, 2024, fourth and fifth graders filled out a short paper survey right after lunch recess. Parents could opt their children out, and none did.

Students answered two questions. One asked how hard they had been breathing (not at all, a little, or a lot), a stand-in for effort. The other asked how hot they felt: “not at all hot,” “a little hot,” or “a lot hot.” In all, 170 students completed 981 surveys, between two and 11 each. Air temperatures from nearby weather stations were matched to each recess, ranging from 90 to 108 degrees and averaging about 98. Recess ran 15 to 30 minutes of free play, and shade covered anywhere from 13.5% to 53.9% of the schoolyards, a big difference in how hot a yard can feel.

In 35% of surveys, students said most of recess was spent sitting still, 43% said light activity, and 23% said hard play. Nearly half of responses, 45%, reported the highest heat level.

Students who felt a little or a lot hot reported more active play than those who felt not at all hot. Measured temperature told the same story. Hard play was reported in 21.2% of surveys on days between 95 and 100 degrees, landing between the cooler and hotter extremes. Only 32 surveys came from days below 95 degrees, so the cooler comparison rests on limited data.

Activity also held steady across the six weeks, with no drop-off as hot days piled up. Kids’ heat ratings generally tracked the weather, too, so they seemed well aware it was hot.

Hard Play Held Up Where Earlier Studies Expected a Drop

A Texas study found hard play dropped and shade-seeking rose above about 91 degrees. In Phoenix, hard play stayed at levels similar to those measured in earlier studies at around 86 degrees.

Researchers offered two possible reasons. Recess may be such a rare chance to run around after long stretches sitting in cool indoor spaces that the pull to play outweighs the discomfort. Younger children, ages 9 to 11 here, may also have trouble recognizing heat as a reason to slow down. Kids absorbed in a game might simply not notice the heat until they stop, an idea the study did not test.

Risk from a short recess is also unsettled. At 15 to 30 minutes, outdoor play may be too brief to raise the chance of heat illness much, and the authors note that most healthy children can safely play in a wide range of hot conditions when hydration and recovery are adequately maintained.

Schools Cannot Rely on Kids to Ease Up at Recess in Extreme Heat

Researchers pointed to existing plans, including guidance from the Arizona Department of Health Services and California’s Extreme Heat Action Plan, that put adult-controlled protections such as shade, water access, and schedule flexibility ahead of a child’s own judgment. The authors describe “a potential mismatch between behavior and heat-related risk.” Earlier research in Maricopa County, which includes Phoenix, found that schools within the same district handled hot-day recess very differently. The authors stopped short of naming a temperature at which recess should change, saying firmer guidance needs more evidence.

These fourth and fifth graders felt the heat and kept playing hard. Whether heat drove that effort or the effort drove the heat, the takeaway for schools holds: shade, water, and schedule changes belong in place ahead of the hottest days, because a fourth grader’s judgment at recess is not a safety plan.

text:
In 1890, the legal age of sexual consent in Delaware was seven years old.

Seven.

In 38 American states, it was twelve or younger.

A man accused of sexually assaulting a little girl could escape conviction by arguing that she had consented.

One woman helped change that.

Her name was Helen Hamilton Gardener.

At a time when most American women couldn't even vote, Gardener joined a movement demanding that lawmakers raise the age of consent and offer girls greater protection against sexual exploitation.

What she discovered was horrifying.

Some legislators resisted reform because they feared girls would falsely accuse men. Others insisted that girls matured early enough to consent to sex.

In Texas, opponents argued that working girls might blackmail their employers. Another argument was that Southern chivalry offered women sufficient protection.

These were actual arguments recorded in an 1895 report on legislative opposition.

Gardener refused to remain silent.

She wrote novels exposing the consequences of sexual abuse, published detailed comparisons of state laws, and publicly identified states that refused to strengthen their protections.

She encouraged Americans to question nearly 9,000 state legislators about their positions.

She also fought proposals that would have denied protection to sexually assaulted girls unless they could prove they had been virgins.

And she challenged the supposedly scientific arguments used to portray women as intellectually inferior to men.

Her campaign was part of a much larger movement involving thousands of women, including suffragists, temperance activists and Black reformers.

By 1900, 32 states had raised their age-of-consent thresholds to between fourteen and eighteen.

Gardener subsequently became an influential campaigner for women's suffrage, helping secure President Woodrow Wilson's support for a federal constitutional amendment.

In 1920, she became the first woman appointed to the United States Civil Service Commission.

She died in 1925.

There is something extraordinary about the women who fought these battles.

They had to ask men for permission to protect children from other men, while those same men denied them the right to participate equally in making the laws.

And some of those lawmakers were more concerned about protecting adult men from accusations than protecting little girls from sexual assault.

You don't know if she's a "good woman." Sure, she was faithful, but we don't know what his home life was like.

I had a friend from my college days in the early 1990s, who needed a place to stay for a while in 2010 and 2011, a year and a month in total. I was super nice to her, getting a second bedroom apartment, paying for a few times of a full visit to a hairdresser, getting her hair cut, colored, and styled, got her a small computer so she could look for work, even her weekly boxes of wine and carton of cigarettes, and I paid for it all. I went over $15k in debt over that year, over and above all my spare income, paying for things she needed because she needed help.

How was I rewarded? Constant derision of "men don't worry so much about their hair" (just trying to keep mine neat) and "men don't keep so clean" (just taking daily showers so I didn't annoy my coworkers.) It was constant comments on how she apparently didn't see me as a man. On top of that, she looked for work for a short time, getting a job for all of three weeks once in that whole year, then she took all that money from that job and took a flight to Texas to see another of her friends for three weeks. All the while, I was paying for everything and she wasn't doing squat to pay for her own expenses.

I didn't do it to be rewarded or for any payback, but some gratitude would have been nice. I did expect her to work to support herself at least partially. She didn't even do any cleaning on the shared part of the apartment. She constantly cut me down. She paid for nothing. I will give her the credit that she stayed out on the patio when smoking, at least when I was there.

By outward signs, she gave the appearance of a "good woman." She was courteous and helpful when it was called for. She wasn't hopping around bed to bed. While she was married, she was faithful to her husband, even after he mistreated her. (I learned more about the "why" of his treatment of her later.) 

Yet, in personal dealings, she's selfish, tears down those around her, just takes all the time, readily takes any charity offered to her without real signs of gratitude, never does anything to support her own life. She was anything BUT a "good woman," but few could see it.

It's difficult to see anyone as a "good person" without knowing how they are personally during private times.

text:
🫧Bubble Talk🫧

... yes, it's too early to be talking about the bubble... but is it truly ever too early?

Here are 12 teams near the supposed cut line, based on efficiency and whether I'm buying their at-large case. Teams can shift throughout the season, just because I sell today doesn't mean I won't buy tomorrow!

BUY📈
- Florida State: The Seminoles look like a team whose stock hasn't caught up with how they're playing yet. If the early form holds, there's room to rise well above where most brackets have them, so now is the time to buy.
- Iowa: Iowa's offense gives it a high ceiling in a deep league where good wins will be available all season. Buy now, before the Big Ten schedule turns quality chances into résumé wins.
- Cincinnati: Yes, the Bearcats lost to Minnesota in a tight contest, but they have the profile of a team that grinds its way into the field: tough defense and plenty of chances against the Big 12. They're undervalued right now, and that's a buy signal.
- Providence: The Friars don't have a big win yet, but I think the Big East will offer plenty of chances to get those wins, and buying now beats paying more in January.

HOLD🫸🫷
- TCU: the Horned Frogs are right where they should be: a believable tournament team without a strong case to move up or down yet. Hold until the addition of Robbie Avila proves one way or another.
- SMU: SMU's ceiling is real, but a thinner schedule means fewer chances for wins that change minds. Hold for now; the key games ahead will show whether this is a bubble team or a lock.
- Maryland: The Terps have the talent to climb but haven't earned the jump yet. There's no reason to sell and not quite enough to buy, so hold.
- Arizona State: The Sun Devils have stopped falling but haven't given a reason to buy back in. A tough league means real chances are coming, so hold and see whether they can turn them into wins.

SELL📉
- Ole Miss: Expectations are running ahead of the results, which is a classic sell-high spot. If the cracks we're seeing continue, this stock has room to fall.
- Creighton: The Bluejays' name carries more weight right now than their play does. Until they show they can win the games that matter, we're cashing out.
- Clemson: Clemson's market price assumes a repeat of past success that the early evidence doesn't support yet. Sell before the rest of the market catches on.
- Mississippi State: The Bulldogs face a brutal SEC grind, and nothing so far says they're built to come out ahead of it. Get out before conference play pushes the price down further.

A major Microsoft infrastructure failure has disrupted essential digital services across 74 countries, exposing how dependent the modern world has become on a handful of technology giants.

The bigger concern:

This is no longer simply about emails or office meetings.

When a single technology provider experiences a major failure, businesses, governments, healthcare systems and even other technology companies can find themselves disrupted.

The incident raises three important questions:

1. Are governments and businesses becoming excessively dependent on a handful of American technology companies?

2. Where are the backup systems when critical cloud infrastructure fails?

3. Should digital infrastructure now be treated as strategically important national infrastructure?

Cloud computing offers extraordinary efficiency, but centralisation also creates systemic vulnerabilities.

The lesson is simple: Digital dependence without adequate redundancy is a strategic risk.

The future belongs not just to those who build the biggest technology platforms, but to those who make them resilient.

text:
The Immutable Law of Reciprocity

By Jack David

As my father used to say, “I live to give, to get, to give, to live, to give.”

That’s not a shallow statement. It’s a philosophy, a purpose, and an understanding of one of life’s immutable laws.

Jesus said in Luke 6:38, “Give, and it shall be given unto you.”

And that means so much more than money or material possessions. It means seeing a need and meeting it. It means recognizing that we are blessed with the opportunity to give because we have something to offer, something worth sharing, and the privilege of experiencing the beauty of another day.

When our focus is on our divine DNA, allowing that spirit to breathe and letting the Lord out to play, we begin to recognize opportunities everywhere.

Sometimes it’s a stranger who needs nothing more than a smile. Sometimes it’s a loved one who needs to hear your voice. Sometimes it’s simply an opportunity to give someone a moment of your time.

We don’t have to search for opportunities to give. They present themselves without much effort at all. We simply have to slow down, take a deep breath, focus, and recognize what’s right in front of us.

Each day we get up, make another step along the way, and have another opportunity to do our best. That’s how we progress. That’s how we create something meaningful.

I’m reminded of the sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, whose words on Veterans Day were simple and unmistakable:

“All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!”

Sometimes we need that reminder. Silence and respect are gifts, too. We honor our surroundings, the people around us, and the significance of the moments we share when we conduct ourselves accordingly.

And perhaps that’s one of the most beautiful things we can give another person: respect. Not something that requires an occasion, an invitation, or even a spoken word. Just the awareness of where we are, who we’re with, and the consideration to honor both.

When we wake up and respect what we have, recognize the beauty of the day before us, and appreciate the people and blessings that surround us, we begin with the greatest gift of all.

We don’t give to receive recognition or reward. We give because it’s who we are. We understand that what we put into the world has a way of finding its way back to us.

Be proud of giving. Give freely, give sincerely, and always give your best.

Today, live to give. And remember, sometimes the greatest gift we can offer is simply a little kindness, a moment of silence, or the respect to honor the world around us.

Give, and it shall be given unto you.

Amen.

— Jack David

Lily came to California for rehab and ended up homeless in South Central. She fell asleep at a friend's while he was home. His cousin threw a blanket over her head, broke her nose with his fists and raped her. A stranger offered her a free flight home. Lily stayed. For the dope.

Lily came to California for rehab in Fountain Valley. Orange County. Quiet, safe, boring. The only person she knew in the whole state lived one city over. So she went.

That's how she ended up in South Central. Four months later she's homeless, still using, and spending her nights in underground casinos.

In the video below her nose is still broken. Her voice sounds stuffed up. And this is a week after it happened.

What happened? She went to a friend's place to shower and change. She fell asleep on his couch. She didn't mean to. "I don't like to fall asleep there for certain reasons."

Who walked in? His cousin. The one who is not allowed in that house at all.

What did she wake up to? A blanket pulled over her head. She couldn't see. She didn't know where she was. Then the punches. "That went on for a while."

How bad was it? Her whole eye went black. Her top lip swelled so much it hung over the bottom one. He broke the bone in her nose.

Then what? "After he was done, I stopped fighting, 'cause I'm not trying to get beat up anymore." Then he took off her clothes and raped her.

Why her? "I guess he saw me on the couch and took what he wanted."

Did she leave South Central? No. This week she went back to the gambling spot twice.

Does she like the danger? "There's something about the unknown." A 9 to 5, she says, just bores her.

Some people will say staying there after that is insane. Others will notice she's only now starting to say it out loud: "Maybe I did not deserve waking up to my face being punched in."

A woman with 20-something dogs offered to drive her straight to the airport and fly her home. Lily didn't go. She was waiting to get her dog Biscuit back first.

She got him back a couple of days ago. She's still in South Central.

Will Lily get on that plane, or is South Central going to keep her?

text:
ALARM TO THE UNCONVERTED
By Jospeh Alleine

Continued…

THE NECESSITY OF CONVERSION

It may be you are ready to say, 'What does all this stir mean?' and are apt to wonder why I follow you with such earnestness, still ringing the same lesson in your ears—that you should repent and be converted. But I must say to you, as Ruth to Naomi, 'Entreat me not to leave you, or to return from following after you.' [Ruth 1:16] Were it a matter of indifference, might you be saved as you are, I would gladly let you alone; but would you not have me concerned for you, when I see you ready to perish? As the Lord lives, before whom I am—I have not the least hope of seeing your face in heaven, except you be converted. I utterly despair of your salvation, except you will be prevailed with thoroughly to turn and give up yourself to God in holiness and newness of life.

Jesus said, 'I tell you the truth, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again' [John 3:3], and yet do you wonder why your ministers labor so earnestly for you? Do not think it strange that I am earnest with you to follow after holiness, and long to see the image of God upon you. Never did any, nor shall any, enter into heaven by any other way but this! The conversion described, is not a high attainment of some advanced Christians—but every soul that is saved undergoes this change.

What is it that you count necessary? Is your bread necessary? Is your breath necessary? Then your conversion is much more necessary. Indeed, this is the one thing necessary. Your possessions are not necessary; you may sell all for the pearl of great price, and yet be a gainer by the purchase. Your life is not necessary; you may part with it for Christ, to infinite advantage. Your reputation is not necessary; you may be reproached for the name of Christ, and yet be happy; yes, you may be much more happy in reproach than in repute. But your conversion is necessary; your salvation depends upon it; and is it not needful in so important a matter to take care? On this one point depends your making or marring to all eternity.

But I shall more particularly show the necessity of conversion, in five things—

1. Without conversion, your BEING is in vain.

Is it not a pity, that you should be good for nothing—an unprofitable burden of the earth—a mere wart in the body of the universe? Thus you are, while unconverted, for you cannot answer the end of your being. Is it not for the divine pleasure that you are and were created? Did not God make you for Himself? Are you a man—and have you reason? Then, think how you came into being and why you exist. Behold God's workmanship in your body, and ask yourself for what purpose did God construct this fabric? Consider the noble faculties of your heaven-born soul. To what end did God bestow these excellencies? Was it to no other end than that you should please yourself, and gratify your senses? Did God send men into the world, only like the swallows, to gather a few sticks and mud, and build their nests, and raise up their young, and then die away? The very heathen could see farther than this. Are you so 'fearfully and wonderfully made' [Psalm 139:14], and do you not yet reason with yourself, 'Surely, I was made for some noble and exalted end!'

O man! set your reason a little in the chair. Is it not a pity such a goodly fabric should be raised in vain? Truly you are in vain, except you are for God. It were better you had no being—than not be for Him. Would you serve your end? You must repent and be converted; without this you are to no purpose; indeed, to bad purpose.

You are to NO purpose. Unconverted man is like a choice instrument, which has every string broken or out of tune. The Spirit of the living God must repair and tune it by the grace of regeneration, and sweetly move it by the power of actuating grace, or else your prayers will be but howlings, and all your service will make no music in the ears of the Most Holy. All your powers and faculties are so corrupt in your natural state that, except you be purged from dead works, you cannot serve the living God.

An unsanctified man cannot work the work of God—

[1] He has no SKILL in it. He is altogether as unskillful in the work, as in the word of righteousness. There are great mysteries in the practice, as well as in the principles of godliness. Now the unregenerate do not know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven. You may as well expect him to read—who never learned the alphabet; or look for goodly music on the lute—from one that never set his hand to an instrument; as that a natural man should do the Lord any pleasing service. He must first be taught of God (John 6:45), taught to pray (Luke 11:1), taught to profit (Isa 48:17), taught to go (Hos 11:3), or else he will be utterly at a loss.

[2] He has no STRENGTH for it. How weak is his heart! (Ezek 16:30). He is soon tired. The Sabbath, what a weariness is it! (Mal 1:13). He is without strength (Rom 5:6), yes, dead in sin (Eph 2:5).

[3] He has no MIND to it. He desires not the knowledge of God's ways (Job 21:14). He does not know them, and he does not care to know them (Psalm 82:5). He knows not, neither will he understand.

[4] He has neither due INSTRUMENTS nor MATERIALS for it. A man may as well hew the marble without tools, or paint without colors or brushes, or build without materials—as perform any acceptable service without the graces of the Spirit, which are both the materials and instruments in the work. Almsgiving is not a service of God but of vainglory—if it does not spring from love to God. What is the prayer of the lips without grace in the heart—but the carcass without life? What are all our confessions—unless they are exercises of godly sorrow and sincere repentance? What are our petitions—unless animated with holy desires and faith in the attributes and promises of God? What are our praises and thanksgivings—unless they spring from the love of God, and a holy gratitude and sense of God's mercies in the heart? So that a man may as well expect that trees should speak, or look for motion from the dead, as look for any service, holy and acceptable to God, from the unconverted. When the tree is evil, how can the fruit be good?

Also, without conversion you live to BAD purpose. The unconverted soul is a very cage of unclean birds (Rev 18:2), a sepulcher full of corruption and rottenness (Matt 23:27), a loathsome carcass full of crawling worms, and sending forth a most noxious stench in the nostrils of God (Psalm 14:3). O dreadful case! Do you not yet see a change to be needful? Would it not have grieved one to see the golden consecrated vessels of God's temple turned into quaffing bowls of drunkenness, and polluted with the idol's service? (Dan 5:2-3). Was it such an abomination to the Jews when Antiochus set up the picture of a swine at the entrance of the temple? How much more abominable, then, would it have been to have had the very temple itself turned into a stable or a pig sty; and to have had the holy of holies served like the house of Baal! This is just the case of the unregenerate. All your members are turned into instruments of unrighteousness, servants of Satan, and your inmost heart into a receptacle of uncleanness. You may see what kind of inhabitants are within—by what come out; for, 'out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies' (Matt 15:19). This black troop shows what a hell there is within!

O abuse insufferable! to see a heaven-born soul abased to such vileness; to see the glory of God's creation, the chief of the works of God, the Lord of this lower world, eating husks with the prodigal! Was it such a lamentation to see those nobles—sit desolate in the streets; and the precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, esteemed as earthen pitchers; and those who were clothed in scarlet embrace dunghills? (Lam 4:2,5). And is it not much more fearful to see the only being that has immortality in this lower world and carries the stamp of God, become as a vessel wherein is no pleasure, and be put to the most sordid use? O intolerable indignity! Better you were dashed in a thousand pieces, than continue to be abased to so vile a service!

2. Not only man—but the whole visible CREATION is in vain without conversion. God has made all the visible creatures in heaven and earth for the service of man, and man only is the spokesman for all the rest. Man is, in the world, like the tongue to the body, which speaks for all the members. The other creatures cannot praise their Maker, except by dumb signs and hints to man that he should speak for them. Man is, as it were, the high priest of God's creation, to offer the sacrifice of praise for all his fellow-creatures. The Lord God expects a tribute of praise from all His works. Now, all the rest do bring in their tribute to man, and pay it by his hand. So then, if a man is false, and faithless, and selfish—God is robbed of all, and has no active glory from His works.

O dreadful thought! that God should build such a world as this, and lay out such infinite power, and wisdom, and goodness thereupon, and all in vain! And that man should be guilty, at last, of robbing and spoiling Him of the glory of all! O think of this. While you are unconverted, all the offices of the creatures are in vain to you. Your food nourishes you in vain. The sun holds forth its light to you in vain. Your clothes warm you in vain. Your horse carries you in vain. In a word, the unwearied labor and continued travail of the whole creation—so far as you are concerned—are in vain. The service of all the creatures which drudge for you, and yield forth their strength unto you, with which you should serve their Maker—is all but lost labor. Hence, 'the whole creation groans' (Rom 8:22) under the abuse of unsanctified men who pervert all things to the service of their lusts, quite contrary to the very end of their being.

3. Without conversion, your RELIGION is vain. All your religious performances will be but lost; for they can neither please God nor save your soul, which are the very ends of religion (Rom 8:8; 1 Cor 13:2-3). Be your services ever so costly—yet God has no pleasure in them (Isa 1:14; Mal 1:10). Is not that man's case dreadful, whose sacrifices are as murders, and whose prayers are a breath of abomination? (Isa 66:3; Prov 28:9). Many under conviction think they will set upon mending, and that a few prayers and alms will set all right again; but alas, sirs, while your hearts remain unsanctified your duties will not be accepted. How punctilious was Jehu! and yet all was rejected because his heart was not upright (2 Kings 10 with Hos 1:4). How blameless was Paul! and yet, being unconverted, all was but loss (Phil 3:6-7). Men think they do much in attending to God's service, and are ready to set Him down as their debtor; whereas their persons being unsanctified, their duties cannot be accepted.

O soul! do not think when your sins pursue you, that a little praying and reforming your ways will pacify God. You must begin with your heart. If that is not renewed, you can no more please God than one who, having unspeakably offended you, should bring you the most loathsome thing to pacify you; or having fallen into the mire, should think with his filthy embraces to reconcile you.

It is a great misery to labor in the fire. The poets could not invent a worse hell for Sisyphus than to be ever toiling to get the stone up the hill, and then that it should presently roll down again and renew his labor. God threatens it as the greatest temporal judgments, that they should build and not inhabit, plant and not gather, and that their labors should be eaten up by strangers (Deut 28:30,38-41). Is it so great a misery to lose our common labors, to sow in vain, and to build in vain? How much more to lose our pains in religion—to pray, and hear, and fast in vain! This is an undoing and eternal loss.

Be not deceived; if you go on in your sinful state, though you should spread forth your hands—God will hide His eyes; though you make many prayers—He will not hear (Isa 1:15). If a man without skill set about our work, and spoil it in the doing, though he take much pains, we give him but small thanks. God will be worshiped after the due order. If a servant does our work—but quite contrary to our order, he shall have stripes rather than praise. God's work must be done according to God's mind, or He will not be pleased; and this cannot be, except it be done with a holy heart.

4. Without true conversion your HOPES are in vain. 'The hope of the hypocrite shall perish' (Job 8:12-13). 'The Lord has rejected your confidences' (Jer 2:37).

[1] The hope of comfort here is vain. It is not only necessary for the safety—but the comfort of your condition, that you be converted. Without this, you shall not know peace (Isa 59:8). Without the fear of God you cannot have the comfort of the Holy Spirit (Acts 9:31). God speaks peace only to His people and to His saints (Psalm 85:8). If you have a false peace continuing in your sins, it is not of God's speaking, and therefore you may guess the author. Sin is a real sickness (Isa 1:5), yes, the worst of sickness; it is a leprosy in the head (Lev 13:44); the plague in the heart (1 Kings 8:38); it is brokenness in the bones (Psalm 51:8); it pierces, it wounds, it racks, it torments (1 Tim 6:10). A man may as well expect ease when his diseases are in their full strength, or his bones out of joint, as true comfort while in his sins.

O wretched man, that can have no ease in this case but what comes from the deadliness of the disease! You shall have the poor sick man saying in his wildness, he is well; when you see death in his face, he would be up and about his business, when the very next step is likely to be to his grave. The unsanctified often see nothing amiss; they think themselves whole, and cry not for the physician; but this only shows the danger of their case.

Sin naturally breeds diseases and disturbances in the soul. What a continual tempest is there in a discontented mind! What a corroding evil is inordinate care! What is passion—but a very fever in the mind? What is lust—but a fire in the bones? What is pride—but a deadly dropsy? What is covetousness—but an insatiable and insufferable thirst? What is malice and envy—but venom in the very heart? Spiritual sloth is but a scurvy in the mind, and carnal security a mortal lethargy. How can that soul have true comfort which is under so many diseases? But converting grace cures, and so eases the mind, and prepares the soul for a settled, standing, immortal peace. 'Great peace have those who love your law, and nothing shall offend them' (Psalm 119:165). They are the ways of wisdom, which afford pleasure and peace (Prov 3:17). David had infinitely more pleasure in the Word, than in all the delights of his court (Psalm 119:103,127). The conscience cannot be truly pacified until soundly purified (Heb 10:22). Cursed is that peace which is maintained in a way of sin (Deut 29:19-20). Two sorts of peace are more to be dreaded than all the troubles in the world—peace with sin—and peace in sin.

[2] The hope of salvation hereafter is in vain. This hope is most injurious to God, most pernicious to yourself. There is death, despair, and blasphemy in this hope.

There is DEATH in it. Your confidence shall be rooted out of your tabernacles, God will destroy it—root and branch; it will bring you to the king of terrors (Job 18:14). Though you may lean upon this house, it will not stand—but will prove like a ruinous building which, when a man trusts to it, falls down about him (Job 8:15).

There is DESPAIR in it. 'Where is the hope of the hypocrite when God takes away his soul?' (Job 27:8). Then there is an end forever of his hope. Indeed, the hope of the righteous has an end—but it is not a destructive—but a perfective end. His hope ends in fruition, others in frustration. The godly may say at death, 'It is finished'; but the wicked, 'It is perished', and may earnestly bemoan himself, as Job did, though mistakenly, in his case, 'Where now is my hope? He has destroyed me; I am gone, and my hope is removed like a tree' (Job 19:10). 'The righteous has hope in his death' (Prov 14:32). When the body is dying, his hopes are living; when his body is languishing, his hopes are flourishing; his hope is a living hope—but others a dying, yes, a damning, soul-undoing hope.

'When a wicked man dies, his expectation shall perish; and the hope of unjust men perishes' (Prov 11:7). It shall be cut off and prove like a spider's web (Job 8:14) which he spins out of his own bowels; but then comes death and destroys all, and so there is an eternal end of his confidence in which he trusted. 'The eyes of the wicked shall fail and their hope shall be as the giving up of the spirit' (Job 11:20). Wicked men are fixed in their carnal hope, and will not be beaten out of it; they hold it fast, they will not let it go—but death will knock off their fingers. Though we cannot undeceive them, death and judgment will. When death strikes his dart through your liver, it will ruin your soul and your hopes together. The unsanctified have hope only in this life, and therefore are of all men most miserable. When death comes, it lets them out into the amazing gulf of endless despair.

There is BLASPHEMY in it. To hope we shall be saved, though continuing unconverted, is to hope that we shall prove God to be a liar. He has told you that, merciful and compassionate as He is, He will never save you notwithstanding, if you go on in a course of ignorance or unrighteousness. In a word, He has told you that whatever you are or do, nothing shall avail you to salvation unless you become new creatures. Now, to say God is merciful and to hope that He will save us without conversion, is in effect to say, 'We hope that God will not do as He says.' We must not set God's attributes at variance. God has resolved to glorify His mercy—but not to the prejudice of His truth, as the presumptuous sinner will find to his everlasting sorrow.

Objection: But we hope in Jesus Christ, we put our whole trust in God, and therefore do not doubt that we shall be saved.

Answer: This is not hope in Christ—but hope against Christ. To hope to see the kingdom of God without being born again, to hope to find eternal life in the broad way—is to hope Christ will prove a false prophet. David's plea is, 'I hope in your word' (Psalm 119:81). But this hope is against God's Word. Show me a word of Christ for your hope that He will save you in your ignorance or profane neglect of His service, and I will never try to shake your confidence.

God rejects this hope with abhorrence. Those condemned by the prophet went on in their sins; yet, says the prophet, 'will they lean upon the Lord' (Mic 3:11). God will not endure to be made a prop to men in their sins. The Lord rejected those presumptuous sinners who went on still in their trespasses and yet would stay themselves on Israel's God—as a man would shake off the briers that cleave to his garment.

If your hope is worth anything, it will purify you from your sins (1 John 3:3)—but cursed is that hope which cherishes men in their sins.

Objection: Would you have us despair?

Answer: You must despair of ever coming to heaven as you are, that is, while unconverted. You must despair of ever seeing the face of God without holiness. But you must by no means despair of finding mercy upon your thorough repentance and conversion. Neither may you despair of attaining to repentance and conversion in the use of God's means.

David loved God. He really, really did.  All the pagan gods had temples. 
David wanted his humble God to have a beautiful temple.
David was thinking laterally.  His only reference was this earth - that is as good as it gets, right? 

Wrong.

GOD always planned to make a temple out of us.
Something alive.
Breathing.
Dimensionally expanded and different than a brick and mortar building.

We HAVE NO IDEA what God has in mind, but we can be certain it is dimensionally above what we are capable of imagining.

The connection you’re drawing is strong and precise.

David sees the surrounding nations with their temples and wants one for the God who has been with him. God answers by refusing the cedar house and instead promising something larger: a house (dynasty/kingdom) established forever, and a place where His people can dwell securely. The language is concrete — “one of your sons, of your own flesh and blood,” “I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever,” “your house and your kingdom shall be established forever.” God makes the promise knowing every future failure of the line. The unconditional character is right there in the text.

1 Peter 2 takes the same theme and relocates the dwelling. The rejected-but-chosen Stone becomes the cornerstone of a spiritual house made of living stones. The people themselves — alive, breathing, indwelt — are the intended dwelling. That is dimensionally different from anything David could have pictured from the reference points available to him.

text:
Scientists Discover a Hidden Weakness in One of the Deadliest Cancers | Temple University Health System & Vincent L, SciTechDaily

Researchers have identified another potential approach to treating pancreatic cancer, with early experiments suggesting that blocking a protein could slow tumor growth and strengthen immune defenses.

Pancreatic tumors can be surrounded by tissue so dense that it compresses blood vessels, making it difficult for nutrients to reach cancer cells. Even under these conditions, the cells continue growing. How they obtain the materials needed to survive has remained an important question.

Researchers at Fox Chase Cancer Center have identified one way pancreatic cancer cells obtain cholesterol and other fats, known as lipids. Their study, published in Nature Cancer, also identified a protein that helps control this process and could offer a potential target for cancer treatment.

The research focused on pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the most common type of pancreatic cancer. These tumors contain large numbers of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), cells that produce and organize connective tissue. As CAFs and their collagen fibers expand, they can compress nearby blood vessels, restricting the tumor’s blood supply.

Cells that restrict blood flow also feed tumors

Despite contributing to this nutrient shortage, CAFs also help cancer cells overcome it.

“We found that CAFs can act as a source of these nutrients,” said Edna Cukierman, PhD, a professor and co-leader of the Cancer Signaling and Microenvironment Program at Fox Chase and co-senior author of the study. “Using laboratory and animal models, we discovered that CAF units acquire cholesterol from the bloodstream and transfer it to nearby pancreatic cancer cells through a process called trogocytosis”

Trogocytosis occurs when one cell takes small pieces of another cell’s membrane during direct contact. In this case, pancreatic cancer cells acquire pieces of CAF membranes containing cholesterol and other lipids that support their survival and growth.

The researchers discovered that this transfer depends on a protein called anoctamin 6 (ANO6), which helps prepare the CAF membrane for the exchange.

“These findings help explain how pancreatic cancer cells obtain essential nutrients despite the unusual structure of the pancreatic tumor microenvironment,” said Igor Astsaturov, MD, PhD, a professor at Fox Chase and co-senior author of the study. “Cancer-associated fibroblasts are not passive bystanders. They actively support tumor growth by transferring lipids to cancer cells.”

When researchers reduced or eliminated ANO6 in CAFs, the cells became less effective at supporting pancreatic cancer cell survival. In mouse models, tumors supported by CAFs with functional ANO6 grew substantially faster than those without functional ANO6.

Cholesterol may exhaust cancer-fighting T cells

The same nutrient transfer process also appeared to interfere with the immune system.

Cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) are immune cells that recognize and kill cancer cells. When these T cells come into contact with CAFs, they can acquire membrane material containing cholesterol. Excess cholesterol in the tumor environment can contribute to T-cell exhaustion, making these immune cells less effective at fighting cancer.

“With Serge Fuchs, professor at the University of Pennsylvania and co-author on the paper, we were surprised to find that the same cellular mechanism can benefit the tumor in two ways – by supplying cancer cells with lipids while also weakening cancer-fighting T cells,” said Astsaturov. “Targeting ANO6 could potentially disrupt both of these tumor-supporting functions at the same time.”

In mouse models, blocking ANO6 reduced cholesterol accumulation in T cells within tumors and improved markers of their activity. Laboratory experiments also showed that T cells exposed to CAFs with reduced ANO6 were better able to kill cancer cells.

Two drugs reduce tumor weight in mice

The researchers then tested whether drugs that interfere with ANO6-dependent activity could slow tumor growth. In mouse models, treatment with niclosamide or clofazimine significantly reduced tumor weight. Niclosamide also reduced cholesterol delivery to pancreatic cancer cells.

These findings suggest that targeting ANO6 could both restrict a nutrient source for pancreatic tumors and improve the immune response against them. However, the results remain preclinical, and further research is needed to determine whether selectively blocking ANO6 would work as a treatment in patients.

Trogocytosis is also only one of several ways pancreatic cancer cells may obtain lipids. The researchers suggest that the drugs tested could potentially help treat other difficult cancers, although that possibility requires further investigation.

“We believe our findings identify ANO6 as a potential therapeutic target that could simultaneously disrupt the nutrient supply supporting pancreatic cancer cells and reduce the immune-suppressive effects of the tumor microenvironment,” said Astsaturov.

The findings also build on nearly a decade of research into how the tissue surrounding pancreatic tumors supports cancer growth.

“Excitingly, reducing ANO6 expression also disrupted the stromal synapse-mimicry circuit we previously identified, which coordinates tumor nutritional support, CAF-unit metabolism, and immune suppression. These findings position ANO6 as the missing mechanistic link that unifies nearly a decade of discoveries by our team,” said Cukierman.

text:
Sarvatirth Jatayu Mandir in Taked Budruk (near Igatpuri and Nashik, Maharashtra) is a revered Hindu pilgrimage site known as the spot where the divine bird Jatayu fought Ravana and attained moksha (liberation) in the arms of Lord Rama. [1] (https://t.co/6k2k2nqozD), [2] (https://t.co/VQM5b1MxS6), [3] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff), [4] (https://t.co/GWfEJqByiV)

History & Mythology

• The Ramayana Connection: According to tradition, when Ravana abducted Goddess Sita, the demigod eagle Jatayu intercepted and fought him bravely. Ravana clipped Jatayu's wings, and the wounded bird fell at Taked. [1] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff)
• The Sarvatirth Kund: When Lord Rama found the dying Jatayu, he held him on his lap and struck the earth with an arrow to draw sacred water. This created an unending natural water spring known as Sarvatirth Kund, which is believed to combine the merits of all sacred waters. [1] (https://t.co/6k2k2nqozD), [2] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff)
• Lord Rama's Rites: Rama performed the final rites and granted moksha to Jatayu right at this location. [1] (https://t.co/bAprP3K3tY), [2] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff)

Temple Complex & Specialties

• Main Statues: The central shrine features an emotional and rare depiction of Lord Rama cradling Jatayu in his lap, accompanied by Lakshmana and Sita. [1] (https://t.co/mxaxJ25gmm)
• Associated Shrines: The larger complex houses temples dedicated to Lord Shiva (including a unique Manakameshwar underground/recessed Shivling tradition), Dattatreya, Satyai Mata, and a south-facing Hanuman. [1] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff), [2] (https://t.co/mxaxJ25gmm)
• The Wishing Stone: A traditional touchstone or Shila inside the premises is traditionally tested by devotees lifting it with focused intent for fulfillment of wishes. [1] (https://t.co/1k2CytqQ5x)
• Perennial Water Flow: The natural spring near the Kund flows continuously year-round. [1] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff)

Atmosphere & Gatherings

• Peaceful & Rural Setting: Nestled in the quiet, scenic foothills and remote landscapes of the Igatpuri-Nashik belt (surrounded by minor forts like Aad, Aundha, and Bitanggad), the temple offers a deeply tranquil, meditative ambiance away from heavy urban noise. [1] (https://t.co/qp4fY8fDbJ), [2] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff)
• Mahashivratri Yatra: The site experiences its largest annual congregation during Mahashivratri, drawing thousands to hundreds of thousands of pilgrims from across Maharashtra. [1] (https://t.co/qp4fY8fDbJ), [2] (https://t.co/LswSV9r2Ff)
You can read more about the regional legends and history of the site via the Jatayu Mandir Overview or check regional travel context on Durgbharari. [1] (https://t.co/cfiojolb5o), [2] (https://t.co/qp4fY8fDbJ)

🇳🇴⚔️🇷🇺Norwegians unveil unmanned trawler designed to hunt Russian submarines in the Arctic.

Norwegian company Kongsberg Maritime has unveiled an unmanned surface vessel (USV) called Arctic Hunter, based on a standard Arctic trawler. It was developed to meet requirements of the UK Royal Navy under the Type 92 program and is offered as part of the "Hybrid Navy" concept (fleets composed of both manned and unmanned platforms).

The project is based on a proven 56-meter hull of a fishing trawler. Engineers have removed all the "fishing" equipment and are installing military hardware. Kongsberg representative Bruce Balchin described the concept in a single sentence: "Replace towing fish with towing a sonar."

The vessel is planned to be equipped with a towed hydroacoustic system Sonar 2087 from Thales UK. This is the sonar already used on British Type 23 frigates.

Specifications (based on publicly available data):

Length: 56 m
Autonomy: Missions lasting up to 60 days at sea
Equipment: Secure military communication, AI accelerator from cortAix, which will use machine learning algorithms to analyze ocean noise faster and more accurately.
-The hull and propellers have been modified to reduce underwater noise.
Manufacturing: Balaena Maritime shipyard in Birkenhead.

Thales UK has already signed a memorandum with Kongsberg for the integration of the sonar and secure communication systems. This project is a continuation of the Lunna House agreement (UK-Norway, December 2025) on NATO leadership in autonomous systems in the North. At the same time, Norway is purchasing at least five Type 26 frigates from Britain.

In the context of a shortage of production capacity and the development of unmanned technologies, combining civilian platforms with military "hardware" appears to be a viable solution. Just six years ago, heavy drones in the skies over Europe were a relatively rare sight; today, they are used thousands of times a day. The maritime theater of operations is awaiting a similar transformation. It is important not to miss this moment, given the increasing strategic importance of the Northern Sea Route and the southern directions.

text:
I think Wardogs S3 has a lot of good things going for it and one glaring issue now that I played a handful of rounds last night.

And that is the fact that one decent game of being a transport pilot nets you the Minigun LB. Whereas getting to level 14 Support does take quite a bit more time in comparison. Last night as I said, I played five full rounds. With about half of the time between the five focusing totally on support without doing completely mindless building for the sake of it.

After those roughly 2.5 rounds I hit Support level 9. So it stands to reason that another 2-3 rounds of focusing purely on support should net me Support 14. Which doesnt sound all that bad, except by the second round of the night I was in a game with no less then five enemy minigun LBs on map almost the entire time and it was a miserable experience. It was half way through the third round, when the experience was repeated, that I said 'F it' and went pure support to rush the large hammer.

Now it is worth noting, that at Support Level 5 you unlock the RPG and at Support Level 8 you unlock the Verba. This does help to some degree, but decent pilots are going to evade the Verba most of the time if you're the only one using one. And since they are disposable, you can only carry one at a time unless you load up a truck inventory with them.

The RPG is a somewhat viable option if you can land your shots. Problem is, most people who use them, cannot. At least not with any sort of consistency. Plus it is much more of a hassle to carry in the early levels since early backpacks have very limited storage space. One cant even carry them at all with the configuration of available slots as a RPG round takes up a 1x3 space in your bag. And the most commonly used one at first, is the Scout backpack which offers you a 2x4   storage grid. If you bring two spare rockets, you're looking at enough space left over for a single spare rifle magazine and 0 health items or grenades. So you have to limit yourself specifically to being the anti-air guy with that kit for the most part.

Anyway, I could go on but the tl:Dr is season 3 is good. I just think the correct move would be to make the large hammer unlock vs the minigun LB unlock occur at about the same amount of time.

The plus side, is that with Limited servers being a thing, you can avoid that hassle entirely by playing on those servers until you unlock Level 14 support yourself or enough time has passed that a good portion of players have them unlocked instead.

So if you are just getting into Wardogs Season 3 or plan to get on soon, my pro tip is to avoid Default servers entirely and head straight for Limited servers until you've unlocked the appropriate counters to the armed helis. You'll have a lot more fun to start and you'll be be able to be better equipped when you eventually switch to the Default servers.
