text:
FYI … horrible thing the Somme

**The Battle of the Somme: A Narrative of Attrition and Sacrifice**

In the summer of 1916, as the First World War dragged into its third year of stalemate, the Allies prepared a massive offensive along the Western Front in northern France. The Battle of the Somme, lasting from 1 July to 18 November 1916, was conceived as a joint British-French effort to smash through German lines near the River Somme. Its dual aims were to relieve the crushing pressure on French forces at Verdun and to force a decisive breakthrough against the entrenched German army. Field Marshal Sir Douglas Haig commanded the British Expeditionary Force, while French forces under General Ferdinand Foch operated to the south. What followed became one of history’s bloodiest and most futile campaigns, a grinding contest that cost over a million casualties for gains measured in mere miles.

Preparation began with a week-long artillery bombardment starting on 24 June. More than 1.5 million shells pounded German positions in an effort to destroy barbed wire, collapse dugouts, and demoralize the defenders. Planners believed the barrage would leave the enemy positions shattered, allowing infantry to walk forward almost unopposed. On the morning of 1 July, at 7:30 a.m., the whistles blew. Eleven British divisions—many of them newly raised volunteer “Pals” battalions from towns and factories across Britain and the Empire—climbed from their trenches and advanced across no-man’s-land toward a 15-mile front.

The bombardment had failed. German soldiers, sheltered deep in concrete bunkers, emerged to man machine guns as the British lines advanced in orderly waves. Enfilading fire cut them down in swathes. By nightfall the British had suffered approximately 57,470 casualties, including over 19,000 dead—the single bloodiest day in the history of the British Army. Limited success came only in the southern sector, where French troops and some British units captured villages such as Montauban and Mametz. Further north, around Beaumont-Hamel and Thiepval, entire battalions were annihilated.

The battle settled into a prolonged campaign of attrition. Tactics slowly improved. On 14 July a surprise night attack seized Bazentin Ridge. Fierce fighting raged through woods and villages—Delville Wood, Pozières, High Wood—with Australian, Canadian, New Zealand, and South African troops joining the fray. On 15 September, during the Battle of Flers-Courcelette, the British introduced the tank for the first time in history. These slow, unreliable machines offered a glimpse of future warfare but could not break the deadlock.

Autumn rains turned the battlefield into a quagmire of mud and water-filled shell holes. Men drowned in the sludge; guns bogged down; advances became measured in yards. By mid-November, with snow falling and temperatures dropping, Haig ordered the offensive halted on 18 November. The Allies had advanced roughly seven miles at the cost of some 420,000 British Empire casualties and around 200,000 French. German losses were estimated between 440,000 and 650,000. No strategic breakthrough had been achieved, yet the battle had drawn German reserves away from Verdun and inflicted irreparable wear on their army.

The Somme remains a symbol of industrial-age slaughter: courage and endurance amid unimaginable horror. It forged a hardened British army through bitter experience and revealed the limitations of outdated tactics against modern firepower. In the end, the green fields of Picardy became a vast cemetery, forever marked by the names of the fallen and the enduring memory of a generation sacrificed for inches of ground. The mud of the Somme still echoes as a warning of war’s terrible cost.

Even though it has nothing to do with me personally, this is a terrifying example of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) manipulating human beings.

I intentionally wrote things that would trigger a reaction, let that reaction happen, and then—just as I had planned—neutralized it.

The People’s Liberation Army can turn human beings into machines using electromagnetic wave manipulation.

These people have truly depraved sexual proclivities.

"Babidi-sama" is just as deranged.

Wait, I’m starting to get a strange headache.

Are they trying to interfere because they’re afraid of what might be revealed?

These people have even gone so far as to teleport human excrement here.

You have no choice but to believe it.

This is a true story.

There’s nothing they won’t do.

But because I’m "special," they don’t dare to attack me.

I’m like Majin Buu—they can’t lay a hand on me.

And my soul—let’s just call it "my soul"—

It’s the same soul that once resided in Minamoto no Yoritomo.

It’s the same soul that was in Shin from the series Kingdom.

Yes, it’s the very same soul that belonged to such figures.

I only found this out yesterday.

Minamoto no Yoritomo once sought the aid of the legendary onmyoji (occultist/diviner), Abe no Seimei.

I suppose I must have the protection of someone like that, too. A certain well-known account—which, by the way, is run by an AI—described Minamoto no Yoritomo as one of the most important figures in Japanese history.

So that’s why! It wasn’t by chance that I ended up living in Kamakura—it was destiny.

I spent a lot of time in Kamakura.

"Chocolate Bank" was great.

Everyone was so kind.

I also visited the shop on Komachi-dori.

The chocolate was delicious.

You know, just like Majin Buu from Dragon Ball, I absolutely love chocolate.

I love sweets in general.

I’ll eat anything—Japanese, Western, or Chinese cuisine.

Oh, the takoyaki just arrived.

Court is in recess.

Finished the first piece of takoyaki.

Finished the second piece.

Finished the third piece.

Finished the fourth piece.

Finished the fifth piece.

Finished the sixth piece.

Finished the seventh piece.

Clearing out the bamboo at home.

Hauling it away.

Work done.

Heading back home.

Going out to buy some milk.

Tried to play with the cat.

The cat ran away.

Bought the milk.

Drank a bitter melon (goya) drink.

Tried some honey from China.

Time to digest.

Stay strong.

Absorb it all.

Take it in, just like Majin Buu.

Resuming.

Hey, Babidi.

I’ll give you a million.

And that’s not all.

I’ll lend you ten million.

Want to take the loan?

"(Silence)"

This is a psychological test.

No one’s going to charge you any interest. Why not just take the loan?

If something comes up, you can use the money; if not, you can pay it back interest-free—there’s no downside.

Plus, you get a million yen.

Are you afraid of me?

Are you intimidated by me?

This is just a test—you know I don’t actually have that kind of money, so you could just give any answer.

He’s definitely scared, isn’t he?

If you’re not scared, then argue back!

"Um... uh..."

This guy’s an idiot.

Has his brain melted or something?

Too much dopamine, maybe?

Isn't that a trend lately?

"Dopa-gaki" (Dopamine-addled brat).

I heard it’s so common—too much dopamine—that the term was even nominated for the "Buzzword of the Year" award.

Watching AVs featuring minors—that’d melt your brain with a flood of dopamine, wouldn't it, "Lord Babidi"?

This guy actually ejaculates while watching women defecating.

What a piece of trash.

Don't lie, you moron.

Oh, and now my own genitals are reacting.

How is this even possible?

Ah, never mind—it’s settling down now.

Another test complete.

If they can do this with electromagnetic waves, they could probably mess with the brain, too.

This is the work of the Chinese People's Liberation Army.

Incredible technology.

Considering the distance between China and here, it’s truly something.

I wonder if my brain is okay after being blasted with all these electromagnetic waves.

Let me reveal another one of your perversions.

Actually, if you go to a porn shop, you’ll find your tastes categorized—pretty much everything except for the "mature woman" (milf) genre.

What a creep.

Someone, please introduce this guy to a woman.

Though, even if I offered a finder’s fee, it wouldn't work, would it, "Lord Babidi"?

After all, "Lord Babidi," you’re currently being sued, aren't you? So, as the representative for the plaintiffs, I’ll start by saying that this first court hearing is a relatively light affair.

I am here to convey the voices of the women who were harmed.

Out of respect for their reputations, I will withhold their names.

In what order should I present these?

Perhaps I’ll start from their youth—it’s easier to recall those memories.

Let’s see, this was 37 years ago.

The defendant was in his second year of junior high school.

The girl in question was also in his second-year class.

She was on the soft-tennis team.

What would you do if someone kept getting in the way like this?

They both had feelings for each other.

"Why didn't you ask me to walk home with you when you handed me your headband?"

"Why didn't you invite me over to your place when I came to watch your match?"

"Why didn't you wait for me at the school's main gate when I gave you that towel?"

"Why didn't you ever speak to me inside the school building?"

"Why weren't you there when I came to your classroom? You knew I was there, didn't you?"

"Why wouldn't you take a photo with me during our school trip?"

"You bought a souvenir for me on our class trip, didn't you? Why didn't you ever give it to me?"

"It was so painful for me when I returned your textbook. Just talk to me! Find some courage! I’m the only one ever putting in any effort here."

"You saw me on graduation day, didn't you? If you noticed me, why didn't you say anything? You’ve been thinking about me all this time, haven't you?"

"You even skipped club practice to wait for me near my house—so why didn't you at least send me a letter?"

"You came to my classroom when we were in our third year. Do you even know why I went there?"

"Just once—try taking the initiative and speaking to me yourself!"

After graduating from junior high, the two went to different high schools.

"Babidi-sama" (the defendant) didn't know where she was headed.

But she knew exactly where he was going.

I suppose she must have heard it from someone.

The two had a fateful reunion—but it would also be their final farewell. Well then, let me tell you how the whole thing unfolded.

But first—time to make some dinner.

I’ll whip up some miso soup, have a bowl, eat some natto, and finish off with some rice.

Maybe I’ll treat myself to a Starbucks White Mocha afterward.

This White Mocha, too, holds memories of Babidi-sama...

Even though the feelings were mutual for them...

Even though he received an answer on the 13th...

Ah, so it was a "welcome," was it?

I can’t quite recall when the "heart" part came into play, though.

Court is now in recess.

While we’re on a break, let’s nitpick Babidi-sama’s high school grades.

Actually, never mind—Babidi-sama has committed a major rule violation.

You can’t do that, Babidi-sama.

You know how it works, don’t you?

Once you graduate from junior high, you move on to high school.

To bet a fortune on something as obvious as that—as if it were some brilliant, spot-on prediction—is just a rigged game.

Take that money and go buy yourself a girl.

And then, have her say this to you:

"Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Majin Buu."

That’s right, isn’t it?

"Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo."

That’s how it goes, right?

Wasn’t that from Disney?

Akira Toriyama, the creator of Dragon Ball—he came up with the name "Majin Buu" based on that very phrase, didn’t he?

By the way, Bibbidi is the father of the sorcerer Babidi.

"Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo."

A perfect relay, isn’t it?

Bibbidi, Babidi, Buu.

After Majin Buu, comes Baby, right?

Baby, who seeks to avenge the Tuffle race.

In the Baby arc, he takes his revenge on the Saiyans by possessing Vegeta’s body and battling Goku.

In that arc, Majin Buu ends up merging with Uub and disappearing.

So, I’d vanish, wouldn’t I?

But then again, I’d become one with Uub. You can enter Uub’s consciousness.

Uub possesses a personality that is the exact opposite of Majin Buu—the embodiment of pure evil.

He is a human brought into existence through the special intervention of King Yemma.

Lord Babidi, you’ve caught the attention of King Yemma.

Your fate is sealed—you’re headed straight for Hell, and you’ll never be able to experience love again.

What awaits you in Hell is the ordeal of being roasted by fire.

Something will be brought to light in 2026.

It was in 2026 that the misdeeds of Babidi-sama—along with those of China’s People’s Liberation Army—would be brought to light.

Perhaps 2027 will be the year of judgment.

A time when all the sins that have piled up over the years will finally be judged.

Another trial is set to begin in 2027.

How many more sleeps until 2027?

Today is November 13th.

Forty-eight days to go.

An incredible synchronicity.

Let us return to the courtroom.

Resuming.

This is a story about a fateful reunion.

As Babidi-sama walked across the school grounds, a teammate remarked:

"Hey, the manager from the opposing high school is looking at you."

Babidi-sama looked toward the opposing team's manager.

To his surprise, it was a girl from his junior high days—someone with whom he had shared a mutual affection back then, both of them in the soft-tennis club.

He never imagined she would end up as a manager for a soccer team.

She, too, had been watching him from afar.

But since they were both in the middle of club activities, they couldn't exactly talk in front of the other team members.

The right moment for them to reconnect never arrived.

And then, the match ended.

As Babidi-sama headed back toward the locker room, he spotted that same girl—the one he had once shared feelings with—filling a bottle at the water station.

Seeing her from behind, Babidi-sama caught his breath.

He hesitated, wondering whether he should speak to her.

He even considered calling out to her.

Just then, a voice came from the left—it was another girl, also from the opposing high school’s soft-tennis club.

Babidi-sama thought to himself:

"If I speak to her here, someone might see us together..."

Why, one might wonder, did Babidi-sama think such a thing? It’s because:

"A girl from the soft tennis club at his high school liked Babidi-sama, and he was interested in her, too."

The girl from his junior high school—the one whose feelings were mutual—likely became a manager for the soccer team, hoping she might cross paths with Babidi-sama again.

Otherwise, why would she quit soft tennis just to become a soccer team manager?

"And in the end, you still didn't reach out to her, did you?"

That was the last time the two of them were ever in the same space.

When a class reunion was held, Babidi-sama went, hoping to see her—but she wasn't there.

By the third reunion, there was a chance she might have shown up.

But she was the only one who didn't attend that particular gathering.

That concludes the prosecution's case.

Now, I shall question the defendant.

Defendant, Babidi—

"Why didn't you send her a letter?"

"It wasn't even an option."

Yet, later on, you did send a letter to that girl from your high school soft tennis club—

—the first girl you ever dated.

When you ended up in a long-distance relationship, she told you how lonely she was not being able to see you, and eventually, you two broke up.

After graduating from high school, you sent her a letter, didn't you?

A letter, presumably, in an attempt to get back together.

And yet, you claim it "wasn't even an option."

Are you an idiot?

She was the first girl who ever returned your feelings.

And you failed to cherish her in the slightest.

If there is any saving grace at all, it’s that you kept using the towel she gave you back in junior high—for years and years.

This court is now adjourned.

The second hearing is scheduled for November 15, 2026.

Since there’s a bit of a gap until the next session, I’ll share some of Babidi-sama’s romantic episodes.

Babidi-sama carries some trauma.

Did I mention this before?

He once sought romantic advice online—well, actually, I think I’ll just go ahead and reveal the details of that consultation right here. How did it all begin, back when Babidi-sama was around thirty?

It happened by chance at a convenience store—he’d gone there to buy some lunch.

Which one was it, I wonder? A Lawson, perhaps?

Speaking of Lawson, there’s the "L-Chiki" (fried chicken), isn’t there? And the "Karaage-kun" nuggets.

Babidi-sama ended up buying an L-Chiki.

A "chicken" move for Babidi-sama, in more ways than one.

Actually, come to think of it—speaking of romance—I’m starting to recall some of Babidi-sama’s own "chicken" (cowardly) romantic episodes.

But for now, let’s stick to Lawson.

Looking from the checkout counter, it was the aisle on the far right. (Wait, I’m thinking of Cocokara Fine—Babidi-sama used to go there a lot... you know, the one in Ginza...)

Babidi-sama has a habit of getting in the way, doesn't he?

"Looking from the checkout counter, it was the aisle on the far right. (Wait, I’m thinking of Cocokara Fine—this guy used to go there a lot... you know, the one in Ginza...)" — is that even funny?

I find myself laughing against my will, even though there’s nothing funny about it.

Is this the work of some Taoist master, or perhaps some dark quantum computer?

Even though it’s not funny, my expression shifts on its own while I’m writing this, and I’m forced to laugh.

"If you write things like this, people are going to think you’re out of your mind," Babidi-sama just remarked.

Babidi-sama sure has a loose tongue when it comes to things like this.

And yet, when I try to press him for more, he clams up completely.

If Babidi-sama’s true feelings were ever exposed online, he wouldn’t just face a massive backlash—he’d practically explode and die.

Anyway—not Cocokara Fine, but Lawson—I was in the aisle on the far right, heading toward the checkout, when I happened to glance over.

The cashier’s right hand.

That right hand, holding the money, brushed against Babidi-sama’s palm.

Usually, you’d avoid touching a customer’s palm—I mean, you wouldn’t, right?

When handing over change—surely you’ve received change before?

There’s no way a clerk’s hand would touch your palm while handing you change, right?

Wait—am I wrong?

Anyway, that wasn’t the actual topic of the consultation.

"If you understand how girls feel, tell me why she touched my palm."

That’s what Babidi-sama just asked me.

Fine, I’ll tell you.

It’s gotta be this, right?

"It wasn’t an accident—it was some kind of signal, wasn’t it?"

Go ahead, try to come up with something better than that.

"(Silence)"

Yeah, nothing.

Babidi-sama, you throw the question at me, even though—well, I already know—you have no clue how girls feel.

That’s exactly why things aren’t working out with this girl, Babidi-sama.

Oh, right—that’s what this was about.

The "substance" of Babidi-sama’s love consultation.

This girl at Lawson—oh, by the way...

Ever since that day their palms touched, Babidi-sama has been going to this Lawson every single day.

What is he, a stalker?

He knows exactly when she’s working—during the day—so he makes a point of driving over there.

Just a few minutes away by car, right?

His excuse? He’s there for the "L-Chiki" (fried chicken).

Yeah, right—it’s not really about the chicken, is it?

Could it be mutual?

She isn’t there every single day, so the only way to see her is for Babidi-sama to show up daily.

And the register, too—he specifically targets the one she’s working at.

Well, obviously.

There’s another girl there—maybe a friend of hers?

She works the same shifts.

And this friend? She can’t stand Babidi-sama. For some reason, I dislike her.

Her customer service is actually fine, but I—Babidi-sama—have a bit of a persecution complex.

Or maybe you’d call it a "cold" attitude?

She treated me a bit coldly.

That’s why I, Babidi-sama, dislike this girl who gave me the cold shoulder.

Also, her face isn’t really my type—that’s probably a factor, too.

For the record, she happens to be tall and has a good build—which is my type—but I’ve convinced myself that the girls I actually like are supposed to be "cute."

Though, to be honest, I can’t quite recall exactly what her face looks like.

Anyway—phew, that took a while.

So, here’s the issue I wanted advice on.

One day, this girl—the one I’ve taken an interest in—said something to me.

At the checkout counter, of course.

"Would you like to sign up for a Lawson card?"

I, Babidi-sama, never sign up for these kinds of loyalty cards.

I don’t want my personal information leaking out.

But, since it was a suggestion from this girl I’m interested in...

...I went ahead and said yes.

And then, I started to wonder:

"Why did she ask me if I wanted to sign up for a card?"

I actually asked this on one of those online forums for relationship advice.

The response was brutal.

"You’re a regular customer—of course she’s going to suggest it, isn't she?"

Well, I suppose that’s true.

But for me—Babidi-sama—it’s not that simple.

I just couldn't be sure.

I ended up reading nothing but harsh comments.

You know, the kind that are just pure criticism?

It left me, Babidi-sama, completely traumatized.

I mean, surely no one else is as big an idiot as me to ask about something like this, right?

But isn't it obvious?

She touched my hand, didn't she?

I mentioned that earlier, didn't I?

You wouldn't touch the hand of a customer you dislike, would you?

I mean, you wouldn't—right?

That’s exactly why I, Babidi-sama, was asking for advice in the first place!

Otherwise, since I’m a regular, it would make sense for her to suggest it, wouldn't it?

Maybe I should talk about this now. How things ended with this girl.

But first—there’s that machine at Lawson, the Loppi, right?

The terminal where you can buy movie tickets.

Even though Babidi-sama could have operated it himself, he deliberately asked this girl how to use it.

Finding ways to create a connection like that—that’s just "Babidi-sama’s style."

What was the movie ticket for, again?

It was a Will Smith movie, wasn't it?

Just now, Babidi-sama said to me:

"If you mention Will Smith’s name here, you’re going to get sued."

I mean, he’s a Hollywood star—there’s no way I’d get sued for that, right?

"Explain why you wouldn't get sued," Babidi-sama demanded.

Well, obviously, no one’s going to sue over something like this.

The movie where Will Smith starred alongside his son...

I can’t recall the title right now.

I’ll write it down once I remember.

The Pursuit of Happyness—

was that it?

Anyway, let’s talk about how it ended.

It was around New Year’s, I think.

Babidi-sama decided to do something...

Something that would never even cross anyone else’s mind.

You probably wouldn't guess it—it’s just so bizarre.

He went and bought—of all things—New Year’s greeting postcards.

And he actually tried to write something on them and send them off.

Why didn't he just ask for her contact information like a normal person?

He’s perfectly capable of talking, isn't he?

They were on speaking terms by then, surely.

So, why not just ask?

Honestly, he really should stop with these creepy tactics.

Babidi-sama drove to the Lawson—it was in the morning, I believe.

He’d happened to find out that she worked an early-morning shift—a time when there wouldn't be any other customers around.

That’s the early morning for you.

text:
GROK! Who is Petr Hlavácek? Why is his work profound?

G: Petr Hlaváček (1950–2014) was a Czech footwear expert, researcher, university lecturer, and Dean of the Faculty of Technology at Tomas Bata University in Zlín. His work is widely regarded as profound for bridging prehistoric archaeology, material science, ergonomics, and practical modern applications—especially in diabetic foot care and understanding human technological history through shoes.
He specialized in shoe materials, production, footwear ergonomics (particularly for diabetics), and historical footwear. Key contributions include:
• Ötzi the Iceman’s shoes: He led detailed analysis and exact replicas of the ~5,300-year-old Alpine mummy’s footwear (bearskin soles, deerskin/calf leather uppers, hay insulation in a net of tree bark or similar fibers). Field tests in the Alps showed they offered excellent grip, shock absorption, temperature regulation, and blister resistance—surprising sophistication for the Stone Age. This project was named among Discovery magazine’s top 100 scientific stories of 2003 and drew international attention (including a New Yorker profile). It demonstrated that early humans used specialized cobblers and advanced construction far beyond simple moccasins, and it informed modern design ideas for pressure distribution.
• Other historical reconstructions: He studied and replicated 10,000-year-old sandals from Fort Rock Cave (Oregon), Terracotta Army footwear (China), Byzantine sandals, and other finds from Europe, the Middle East, and elsewhere. He co-authored 10,000 Years of Shoes and documented shoes on ancient statues and icons.
• Modern and applied impact: He contributed to ISO global shoe-size nomenclature, worked on international diabetic-foot guidelines, and researched children’s footwear and ergonomics. Awards included recognition from the International Union of Shoe Industry Technicians (UITIC) and others. Colleagues noted his integrity, constructive approach, and high standards.
His experimental archaeology (building and hiking in replicas) made abstract history tangible and challenged assumptions about prehistoric technology, while his ergonomics work had direct medical relevance.
Note: Several other notable Czechs share the name, including architect and incoming Prague mayor Petr Hlaváček (b. 1961), who has led major urban planning work such as the Metropolitan Plan (enabling substantial housing on brownfields while managing growth), and historian/philosopher Petr Hlaváček (b. 1974), who researches Czech messianism, European identity, and intellectual history. The shoe expert is the one whose research most consistently draws the “profound” label for its interdisciplinary scientific and historical depth.

text:
When Hebrews exhorts us to offer a continuous “sacrifice of praise” (Hebrews 13:15), we instinctively think “sacrifice” is a metaphor. Real sacrifice, we assume, needs blood, flesh, altars, and smoke.

That instinct gets things exactly backwards. Think about Jesus. Jesus offers the true, human sacrifice that atones for sin once-for-all. His blood does what the blood of bulls and goats could never do.

We should apply the same logic to our liturgical “sacrifices.” According to Scripture, the old sacrifices were shadows, faint images of true. What we do is the reality that Israel’s symbolic sacrifices pointed to. In worship, we offer ourselves as living sacrifices in Jesus.

Everything that happened symbolically in Old Testament sacrifice happens in Spirit and truth in Christian song.

Israelite sacrifice was a rite of ascent. Animals ascended as a soothing aroma in Yahweh’s nostrils, as a memorial of His promises. As we sing in the Spirit, we ascend as a sweet-sounding song in His ears, a musical memorial of His promises.

Sacrifice is a ritual of transformation. Animals were translated into sacrificial fire and smoke. In the new covenant, the Spirit fills us so that we sing and make melody in our hearts (Ephesians 5:18-19). Those who are transformed by the Spirit sing, and the Spirit transforms us by song.

Sacrifice is a rite of division and reunion. Animals were dismembered in order to be reconstituted in smoke and fire. In the new covenant, music reunites the cosmos. Song crosses the boundary of the firmament to reunite heaven and earth, as we join with angels and archangels and all the company of heaven (cf. Hebrews 12:18-24).

Song also binds us as one body, each voice making its unique contribution to the complex but united sound of the choir of Christ’s body. Song is a real-world sonic anticipation of the perfect harmony of new Jerusalem. Wherever two or three sing in the Spirit: Behold, there is new creation!

Sacrificial animals re-entered the symbolic Paradise of the temple, passing by the priests with their cherubic swords and fire. Through Jesus, we gain access to the heavenly sanctuary, and as we sing in the Spirit we enter the heavenly courts of Yahweh.

None of this is mere metaphor. We truly ascend to join the heavenly liturgy. We are truly transformed by the Spirit and song. We really are united, physically, as our voices sound through one another’s bodies. Animal sacrifices look solid and real. But they’re mere shadows compared to what happens every Sunday when we sing.

We don’t have the luxury of delegating our sacrifice of praise to professionals. Yes, each member of the church has unique gifts to serve the body. Some lead and exercise authority; some teach; some are shepherds; some are gifted musicians.

But we’re all priests, and that means we all offer the sacrifice of praise. If you sing badly, sing badly, or learn to sing better. Silence isn’t an option. You’re a priest, every last one of you. Singing is your job. It’s one of your main jobs.

– Peter Leithart

——————————

I understand your point, and I appreciate your response. 😊

But my criticism isn't about the technical quality of Crimson Desert. I absolutely love the base game and have already completed it twice.

My problem is that I don't think €25 is justified for an expansion that primarily introduces new mechanics without providing meaningful content to accompany them.

Look at Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty, for example. It offers an entirely new, complex storyline with memorable characters, mysteries, political intrigue, and meaningful decisions. You want to keep playing because you want to know what happens next.

Now look at the ocean expansion in Crimson Desert.

You have ships, naval combat, diving, underwater equipment, new islands, and countless resources to collect. But what is the actual purpose of all these mechanics?

The islands are practically empty. There is no overarching maritime storyline connecting them. The three new character storylines have little to do with the ocean itself, and they are incredibly short.

As an endgame player, I already have around a hundred weapons and more resources than I need. Why should I spend hours sailing, diving, and collecting more materials when there is nothing meaningful left to accomplish?

That's why the ocean expansion feels more like a technical demonstration of what a naval exploration game COULD be, rather than a fully developed expansion.

The technology is impressive. The potential is enormous. But the adventure itself is missing.

And that's precisely why I'm disappointed. Pearl Abyss has already proven with the base game that they can create an incredible world. I simply expected the expansion to offer a new adventure within that world, not just new ways to move around in it...

text:
Some pictures are worth more than a thousand words. These two pictures tell a story that goes far beyond football. They capture the evolution of a young man who once stood on the sidelines receiving instruction and encouragement, eventually becoming the person standing beside another young athlete, offering that same guidance.

The second picture takes me back to my days as a quarterback at Lincoln High School. I was wearing number 5, learning the game, listening to my coach, and trying to make the most of an opportunity. At that point in my life, I had dreams of playing college football and making something of myself. I couldn’t have imagined all the places that journey would eventually take me.

The first picture represents something much bigger. Years later, I found myself on the other side of the game. Instead of wearing the uniform, I was wearing the headset. Instead of receiving instruction, I was providing it. Instead of being the young quarterback looking for direction, I was standing beside another young quarterback wearing number 5, sharing knowledge, building confidence, and helping him navigate his own journey.

The number stayed the same, but the role changed.

That is the beauty of paying it forward.

Football gave me more than an opportunity to compete. It taught me discipline, accountability, perseverance, leadership, and the importance of relationships. It introduced me to people who believed in me, challenged me, corrected me, and invested in my development. Those lessons followed me from Lincoln High School to Louisiana Tech, through my coaching career, into athletic administration, and ultimately to my current role as Executive Director of Athletics for Dallas ISD.

Looking at these pictures reminds me that leadership doesn’t begin with a title. It begins with someone investing in you and your willingness to do the same for someone else.

My journey has come full circle. I went from being a student-athlete to a coach, from a coach to an athletic administrator, and now to a position where I have the opportunity to influence athletics across an entire school district. But regardless of the title, the mission has remained the same: impact lives.

I often think about the young people who cross my path. They may not remember every play, every practice, or every conversation, but I hope they remember that someone believed in them. I hope they understand that their circumstances do not have to determine their destination.

The greatest victory isn’t always found on the scoreboard. Sometimes, it’s found years later when you see the young people you invested in becoming successful adults, leaders, fathers, mothers, coaches, and contributors to their communities.

These pictures remind me that I didn’t just play football. I became part of something bigger than myself. I was blessed to receive opportunities, and now I have a responsibility to create opportunities for others.

The journey continues, but the purpose has never changed.

REACH ONE. TEACH ONE. PAY IT FORWARD.

From wearing number 5 to wearing the headset. From being poured into to pouring into others.

WE GET TO!

FRIDAY MORNING DISPATCH UPDATE

November 13, 2026 | Denver Metro and Front Range

Police, fire and emergency crews responded to numerous incidents overnight and into Friday morning, including multiple highway crashes, reported assaults, weapons calls, domestic disturbances, vehicle fires and transit disruptions.

The following incidents are listed from newest to oldest, based on dispatch timestamps. Times are Mountain Standard Time.

8:08 AM | Scooter Blocks RTD Train

East 40th Avenue, Denver

An eastbound RTD train was forced into an emergency stop after a scooter or bicycle was left dangerously close to the tracks. The train reportedly slowed to approximately 2 mph before stopping. Personnel were requested to remove the obstruction so subsequent trains could proceed.

8:04 AM | Child Possibly Injured in Two-Vehicle Crash

Huron Street and Thornton Parkway, Thornton

Emergency crews responded to a two-vehicle collision in the southbound lanes of Huron Street, north of Thornton Parkway, near a vacant gas station. An 11-year-old reportedly suffered a possible shoulder injury. Engine 72 was investigating.

8:01 AM | Vehicle Strikes Pedestrian Near High School

South Picadilly Street, Aurora

Fire and medical personnel were dispatched to a reported collision involving a vehicle and pedestrian near Crest High School. The pedestrian’s condition was not immediately available.

7:59 AM | Fire Reported Along Westbound Sixth Avenue

Sixth Avenue near Kipling Street

Dispatch traffic indicated a possible fire along westbound Sixth Avenue near Kipling, with traffic backing up in the area. The cause and extent of the fire were not immediately confirmed.

7:49 AM | Purse Stolen During Vehicle Break-In

North Highway 287, Lafayette

Police responded to a fitness center after someone reportedly smashed a vehicle window and stole a purse. Officers were investigating the theft.

7:42 AM | Reported Drug Activity

Broadway and Speer Boulevard, Denver

Officers were dispatched after a report of approximately seven people possibly using narcotics near southbound Broadway and Speer. An additional unit was assigned to provide cover.

7:41 AM | Vehicle Fire Reported Extinguished

Westbound highway shoulder near mile marker 246

Transportation radio traffic indicated a vehicle fire on the westbound shoulder had been extinguished. No traffic blockage was reported.

7:37 AM | Water Flowing From Manhole

West Cannon Place and Sutton Circle, Lafayette

Public Works was notified of water continuing to flow from a manhole near Cannon Place and Sutton Circle. Water was reportedly running down the street.

7:33 AM | Dead Turkey Creates Traffic Hazard

South Havana Street and East First Avenue, Aurora

Public Works received a report of a dead turkey in the roadway, creating a possible traffic hazard. Police notification was discussed.

7:30 AM | SUV Blocking Bus Stop

Wadsworth Bypass

A white Ford SUV was reported parked at a bus stop since the previous day, potentially obstructing access for transit passengers.

7:18 AM | Three-Vehicle Crash

20th Street, Denver

A three-vehicle collision left one vehicle disabled. Crews moved vehicles to the left shoulder and spread sand. No injuries were subsequently reported.

7:08 AM | Welfare Check at Union Station

Union Station, Denver

Transit officers were sent to check on two people appearing to be sleeping or slouched over near an elevator. Surveillance cameras reportedly showed both individuals, and one was said to have a lighter. A cover unit assisted.

7:05 AM | Three-Vehicle Crash Blocks Lane

Westbound I-76 near East 88th Avenue, Commerce City

Colorado State Patrol requested fire and medical assistance after a three-vehicle collision. One lane was blocked. Responders reported minor vehicle damage and that all occupants were outside their vehicles.

7:02 AM | Update on I-70 Vehicle Fire

Westbound I-70 near mile marker 255, Golden

A vehicle involved in an earlier fire was reported on the shoulder, with all travel lanes reopened. Colorado State Patrol continued providing traffic protection.

7:00 AM | Three Vehicles Blocking I-76

Westbound I-76 east of US-85

Three vehicles were reported blocking the left lane. A responding unit requested to turn around and return to the scene. This may relate to the collision reported minutes later near 88th Avenue.

6:53 AM | Trespassing Report Behind Car Wash

Cannon Circle, Louisville

Officers responded to a wooded area behind a car wash following a trespassing complaint. The incident was subsequently reported Code 4, indicating the situation appeared resolved.

6:49 AM | Semi and Truck Collision, One Hospitalized

Airport Boulevard on-ramp, Aurora

A semi and another truck collided on an Airport Boulevard on-ramp. Damage was described as minor, but one person was transported to University Hospital.

6:43 AM | Reported Knife Assault

Green Valley Ranch Boulevard, Aurora

Police and emergency medical personnel responded to a possible knife-related assault. An injured man was reported down the street while a thin adult male suspect reportedly fled the area. The circumstances and extent of injuries remained unclear.

6:43 AM | Fire Alarm at Littleton Police Department

West Berry Avenue, Littleton

South Metro Fire Rescue dispatched Engine 11 to a commercial fire alarm at the Littleton Police Department. No confirmed fire was reported in the available dispatch summary.

6:41 AM | Assault With Injuries

East Exposition Avenue near South Ironton Street, Denver

Emergency crews were dispatched to an apartment following a report of an assault with injuries. Additional information about the victim was not available.

6:36 AM | Assault Victim Requires Medical Assistance

Commerce City, East Street area

Police requested fire and medical assistance for a possible assault victim. Police were already on scene, and the medical response was requested as routine.

6:29 AM | Gun Discovered Under Bed

Lydia Drive, Lafayette

Police responded after a firearm was discovered beneath a bed inside a residence. The reporting party believed the gun belonged to their father and had not been removed from a safe box.

6:28 AM | Road Rage Involving Red Truck

Niwot Road and 107th Street, Boulder County

A driver reported that a red truck attempted to force their vehicle off the roadway while traveling southbound. The truck’s driver was reportedly yelling and swearing. The reporting party was following the vehicle and willing to provide a statement.

6:04 AM | Truck and Grass Fire Closes I-70 Lanes

Westbound I-70 near mile marker 255, Golden

Fire crews responded to a truck pulling a trailer that was fully involved in flames. Fire was reported in the cab and hood, and nearby grass also caught fire.

Lanes two and three were closed while firefighters worked to contain the blaze. A later update indicated the vehicle was on the shoulder and all lanes had reopened.

6:02 AM | Two-Vehicle Crash

East 88th Avenue and Tower Road, Commerce City

A dark SUV and black Toyota Tacoma collided. One person reported neck pain. Both vehicles were off the roadway with minor to moderate damage.

A separate medical call in the dispatch traffic concerned a 46-year-old man with a worsening spider bite on Oneida Street.

5:40 AM | Trespassing Complaint at Dollar Tree

West 84th Avenue, Federal Heights

Deputies were dispatched after an unwanted person was reportedly sleeping outside a Dollar Tree and refused requests to leave. Broken glass was also reported nearby.

5:10 AM | Driver Reports Being Followed

West Colfax Avenue and Brentwood Street, Lakewood

Police responded after a caller reported a vehicle repeatedly honking, flashing its lights and following them.

4:59 AM | Hit-and-Run Involving Two SUVs

Interstate 25

4:58 AM | Possible RTD Bus Collision

C-470 interchange

Transportation personnel received a report involving a possibly disabled RTD bus and another vehicle. The bus was reportedly attempting to cross multiple traffic lanes, prompting a request for someone to investigate.

4:53 AM | Assault at Old Town Arvada Parking Garage

Vance Street, Arvada

Mile marker 259, reported East Colfax area

East 10th Avenue area, Denver

3:56 AM | Bus Crash

Westgate and 43rd Avenue area, Denver

3:27 AM | Woman Reportedly Pulled Into Apartment

West 10th Avenue, Lakewood

Police responded after a witness reported hearing a woman yelling for help and seeing a man pull her back into an apartment. No weapons were reported. The woman’s condition was not available.

3:26 AM | Traffic Stop

1600 Block of Pierce Street, Lakewood

3:01 AM | Police Search for Armed Shooting Suspect

South Federal Circle, Littleton

Police issued information about a suspect sought in connection with a reported shooting near South Federal Circle around 1:09 AM.

The person was believed to be armed and associated with a white sedan displaying temporary registration tags. Officers were instructed to contact Littleton police if the suspect was located.

2:43 AM | Armed Suspect Bulletin

400 Block of South Federal Circle, Littleton

2:32 AM | Pickup Strikes Railroad Crossing Barrier

East 40th Avenue and York Street, Denver

A white pickup reportedly struck a median and railroad crossing arm. Officers were checking the scene and reviewing camera footage.

2:20 AM | Man Seriously Injured in Possible Assault

North Iola Street and East 17th Avenue, Aurora

Emergency crews responded to a 52-year-old man who was conscious and breathing but reportedly vomiting, unable to stand and having difficulty seeing.

Dispatch information suggested he may have been struck in the head and subsequently hit his head on the floor. There was also an unclear reference to a knife.

2:17 AM | Wrong-Way Driver on Highway 6

Highway 6 near Wadsworth Boulevard, Lakewood

2:04 AM | Assault at Apartment

West 58th Avenue, Arvada

Medic 52 was dispatched to a reported assault at an apartment in the West 58th Avenue area. Responders were instructed to stage nearby.

2:02 AM | Repeated Noise Complaint

South Teller Street, Lakewood

Officers responded after a caller complained about an upstairs neighbor making loud noises resembling objects being dropped. Dispatch referenced previous disturbances at the location, including a possible firearms-related incident.

2:00 AM | Juvenile Reportedly Took Pills

East Mississippi Avenue area, Aurora

Emergency crews were dispatched after a report that a juvenile male had taken pills in a park. Responders were directed to the north side of the park. The dispatch headline described him as conscious.

1:58 AM | Possible Overdose at Aurora City Park

9701 East 16th Avenue, Aurora

Fire and police responded to a possible overdose at Aurora City Park near Dayton Street. The patient’s condition was not immediately available.

1:38 AM | Two Assault Reports

Motel 6, 9920 West 49th Avenue, Wheat Ridge, and West Third Avenue near Living Parkway

Emergency dispatch traffic referenced two separate reported assaults. One occurred at a Motel 6, and the other near West Third Avenue and Living Parkway. Medical personnel were instructed to stage nearby.

Table Mesa Drive and South Broadway, Boulder

1:18 AM | Screaming and Breaking Glass Reported

West Kentucky Avenue, Denver

Officers responded after a caller reported hearing screaming, someone shouting “grandma help,” banging and glass being thrown at a residence. Additional units were dispatched.

1:00 AM | Police Check Hotel Room

Kipling Street, Lakewood

12:46 AM | Disabled Bus

South Tower Road and East Louisiana Avenue, Aurora

Transportation dispatch received a report of a disabled bus. Units from the East Metro area were responding, and additional coverage was requested.

Garrison Street, Lakewood

Police responded to an apartment disturbance involving several reportedly intoxicated adult men who refused to leave. The incident was described as no longer physical, with no weapons reported.

E-470 near Peoria Meadows

Emergency crews coordinated traffic control and shoulder access following a reported rollover crash. Responders discussed moving the roadway closure point closer to a pedestrian bridge.

11:50 PM | Serious Injury Crash

Southbound I-25 at C-470

Van Gordon Way, Westminster

11:46 PM | Repeated Apartment Noise Complaint

West 14th Avenue, Lakewood

Officers responded after a caller made multiple complaints about loud noise at an apartment. Dispatch discussed providing responding officers with a building access code.

11:45 PM | Open 911 Call

West Mansfield Parkway, Lakewood

Northbound I-25 near E-470

Lee Hill Drive, Boulder

Golden Eagle Circle, Golden

South Sheridan Boulevard, Lakewood

AMERICA WEEK EPISODE 88  (VIDEO IN ITALIAN, TEXT IN ENGLISH)
By Stefano Vaccara
NEW YORK (ITALPRESS) – This week in America feels like something straight out of a movie. A Chinese spy, a billionaire brought down by sex scandals, Wall Street trembling, a Defense Secretary under fire, and a president who can feel the walls closing in around the White House.
Let's start with the spectacular downfall of #JensenHuang, the founder of #Nvidia, the microchip giant powering artificial intelligence. A company that reached a valuation of $5.7 trillion, becoming one of the driving forces of both the American and global economies.
#Huang resigned following revelations of two extramarital affairs. One with Alice Huang, a businesswoman suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China. The other with an executive at Nvidia itself. The company's stock plunged, sending shock waves through Wall Street and the entire technology sector.
Nvidia, after all, controls roughly 90 percent of the market for advanced AI chips. According to The New York Times, Trump had been warned by U.S. intelligence agencies and even by Secretary of State Marco Rubio about suspicions surrounding the alleged Chinese spy, yet he took no action. Meanwhile, Huang continued visiting the White House and influencing American policy on technology exports to Beijing. Now Congress wants to know what the president knew and why he failed to act.
Another potential investigation added to the growing list awaiting the Trump administration. Because the blue tsunami unleashed by the midterm elections continues to send shock waves across America.
The latest, a historic one, comes from Mississippi, where #ScottColom defeated Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith, becoming the first Black senator elected from that state since Reconstruction, more than 150 years ago.
Mississippi, the land of segregation and the long struggle for voting rights, is sending a Black Democratic senator to Washington.
A victory that reveals just how profoundly America is changing, and Trump knows it.
In January, Democrats will take control of Congress, armed with investigative committees, subpoena powers, and the ability to compel sworn testimony. Investigations that could reach directly into the president's affairs, his family, and his entire inner circle.
Meanwhile, Pete Hegseth, the head of the Pentagon, has managed to freeze impeachment proceedings against him, at least for now. A reprieve that may last only until the new Congress takes office.
Even at Arlington National Cemetery, a military guard had to shout at the Secretary of "War" and his laughing entourage, ordering them to show respect and remain silent in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The video went viral.
Above all, there are still the Epstein files, with mounting pressure to reveal everything the Justice Department has yet to make public.
Trump is reacting the way he always has: by attacking.
In words, he offers cooperation to Democrats. In practice, he promotes Stephen Miller, the architect of his mass deportation policies, to White House chief of staff and orders Vice President JD Vance to investigate alleged corruption in Democratic-run states.
Corruption, of all things!
It looks almost like a preemptive reflex: accuse your opponents of the very wrongdoing you fear they may soon investigate you for.
Rather than a lame duck, Trump increasingly resembles a hunted fox. He senses his pursuers closing in and bares his teeth, convinced he can still frighten them away.
Yet this is precisely where he may be making his biggest mistake: the new Democrats arriving in Congress are not the same politicians who spent years seeking compromises with Trumpism.
Take Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan's newly elected senator. He has made his position unmistakably clear: deference doesn't work with a bully. You have to confront him with even greater force, because a bully backs down when he discovers that someone is no longer afraid of him.
Then there's Bernie Sanders, an independent senator who is already leading a revolt against Chuck Schumer, the symbol of an old Democratic leadership accused of making too many concessions to Trump.
The battle to replace the party's leadership has begun, as a new generation of Democrats wants to move from resistance to the offensive.
Of course, Trump is also desperately searching for political breathing room, pushing for an agreement on Ukraine or Iran. But at this point, even a diplomatic breakthrough seems unlikely to stop the accountability process that the incoming Congress has already pledged to pursue.
Some argue that Democrats should focus more closely on the mandate voters gave them, concentrating exclusively on the cost of living and leaving investigations behind.
It's a false choice, especially since concern over rampant corruption in Washington was among the top priorities of voters who backed the Democrats.
American voters have come to understand that when corruption shapes government decisions, ordinary people's standard of living pays the price as well.
Trump may no longer be able to intimidate Democrats, but how much power will he have left when he discovers that his threats no longer work?
Trump built his power on other people's fear.
Starting in January, he will have to learn to live with his own.

text:
"You think these kids should care that a society sold them a lie and then indebted them to the lie and then told them they are on their own?"

What is the lie?  And how did society indebt them? 

Further, having kids of this age, and recently participating in about 6 campus tours across the Eastern US, something became painfully obvious to me.  

Good luck if you want to get into a Wake Forest, Carnegie Mellon, Penn State, Duke, William and Mary, Penn...etc.. 

The number of applicants are in the tens of thousands more than some of these schools accept.  My question is why? There are dozens, even hundreds of schools in this same East Coast geography that offer basically the same education at a fraction of what these schools charge.

Kids don't want these other schools because they want the "brand name" the sweatshirt...etc.. which is basically 2x or 3x the price.

This is on the parents and the young adults. Back in my day, you wanted a good education and it didn't matter what the brand was.

Now, it's a social construct.  You blame it on free money and lies.  I say we've lost the basic ability to calculate what a $80K / year education gets us from university X while university Y is right down the road for $18K.  

As a former large employer, I can tell you I didn't care what the brand was on any of the hundreds of people I hired. I cared if they had the skills to do the job I was hiring for. 

I go back to my original stance that if someone is showing up at my doorstep with $200K in debt for a degree they should have paid $70K for, I am already doubting  if they have the pedigree to make other complex decisions. 

There should be a mandatory HS class for anyone on a college track to help them with the relationship between where they want to attend college, what it costs, and what the jobs in that field pay upon completion of college.  You have kids getting 4 year psychology degrees from $80K a year institutions and then wondering where it all went wrong upon graduation.

text:
Oracle-powered programs deliver record 1 GW in peak demand cuts for US utilities | Aamir Khollam, Interesting Engineering

Electricity demand can surge during extreme temperatures, putting additional pressure on power grids. US utilities are increasingly turning to customers themselves to help manage those peaks. Oracle says its utility programs have delivered a record 1 gigawatt (GW) of peak demand reduction across North America in 2026.

The company’s Opower platform supported 73 demand response events across winter and summer. Those efforts involved 4.3 million customers across participating utilities. The total demand reduction equals the output of more than three peaker power plants in Washington state.

Customers help balance grid demand

Oracle’s Opower platform uses behavioral demand response (BDR) and peak-time rebate (PTR) programs. These initiatives encourage households to shift electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Customers can receive personalized messages explaining when and how to reduce their usage.

The approach also expands virtual power plants (VPPs) beyond households with connected devices. Utilities can draw on participating customers’ flexible electricity consumption to reduce pressure on the grid. Some programs also offer financial rewards for reducing usage during designated peak periods.

Oracle reported that utilities conducted 73 events in 2026, compared with 49 last year. That represents an increase of nearly 50%. Average peak demand savings reached 16,592 kilowatts per event, equivalent to the peak electricity needs of approximately 4,150 homes.

Customer participation also climbed significantly. The programs reached 4.3 million customers, up from 3.3 million in 2025.

Utilities expand demand response

Puget Sound Energy (PSE) has incorporated Oracle’s BDR program into its virtual power plant strategy. Its Flex Events initiative uses customer communications to encourage temporary reductions in electricity consumption.

The program combines text messages, interactive voice calls, and email outreach. PSE reported peak load reductions of up to 16.6 megawatts (MW) during individual events across three consecutive deployment seasons.

Earlier in 2026, PSE introduced performance-based incentives to encourage greater participation. Customers can now receive a $0.50-per-kilowatt-hour bill credit for reducing electricity consumption during qualifying events.

“We’re excited to continue partnering with Oracle to design customer-focused solutions that are easy to participate in,” said Tom Smith, PSE’s supervisor for demand response.

CPS Energy also reported strong participation across its service area in San Antonio, Texas. More than 350,000 customers joined its behavioral demand response programs. That represents over one-third of its customer base.

The utility conducted 12 demand response events during summer. Participation helped deliver nearly 19 MW of peak demand reduction during August.

Programs target winter peaks

Oracle has also expanded its demand response offerings to support year-round events. Utilities can now use these programs during winter storms and other periods of elevated electricity consumption.

The expansion addresses changing electricity demand patterns across the United States. Some regions increasingly experience their highest grid demand during winter. Flexible customer participation gives utilities another way to manage those seasonal pressures.

Opower also allows utilities to target different customer groups with tailored messages. This gives households more relevant guidance based on their participation and energy programs.

Behavioral demand response and peak-time rebates are becoming important tools for managing electricity consumption. Their growing reach could help utilities access flexible capacity across more households. That capacity may prove increasingly useful as US electricity demand puts greater pressure on existing grid infrastructure.

Maria Teresa Rodriguez is the concerned parent who asked questions of the Islam religion display in the Catholic girls' high school in Louisville, KY 
Assumption High School.
"I had my meeting with the school and I want to share how it went, point by point my concerns and the answers I received.
First, I want to encourage every parent who has concerns about the education our girls are getting to please reach out to the school and not be afraid to speak up. I am a Catholic mother paying for my children to be formed in our faith, not despise it.
To those who didn’t like me questioning AHS:
It's sad to see the ugliness of some of you, just because I was concerned with what I saw, what type of education would my daughter be getting and wanting answers.
Concerns came up, and suddenly the craziest ideas are made up about me just because we disagree politically.
I didn't know I wasn't allowed to question a prospective school where my daughter was supposed to go and where we would be spending thousands of dollars.
I didn't know it was prohibited to speak up when I didn't like something.
The same people who preach love and acceptance can't accept when someone disagrees with them and challenges an institution to be better and to do better for our children.
I was not being unreasonable. I’m not asking the school to hide the world from my daughter. I am asking a Catholic school to be Catholic.
Here is how the meeting went:
I asked: A Catholic school chose to hold up socialist leaders and Islamist figures as role models for young girls. That is not neutral education for a display is an endorsement. How does presenting these figures as role models align with Assumption's Catholic mission, and who approved it?
They answered: 

The Catholic school curriculum is approved by the Archdiocese.

 The girls learn about different religions. 

They also said 
the school is sponsored by an order, the Sisters of Mercy, whose focus is social justice. 

Some orders are not as conservative as others.
On students writing Islamic words and citing the Quran:
I said: I accept a Catholic curriculum that teaches about other religions. What I object to is students writing out Islamic words and citing the Quran in a way that embraces that ideology. Catholic girls should not be asked to produce work that confesses another faith. Where is the line at this school between teaching about a religion and having students practice it?
They answered: The Islam and world religion material is built around a book about a refugee family and what they had to go through, and it teaches the girls what women's role in that religion is. The calligraphy on the wall is the focus of the project because Muslims don't have symbols, calligraphy is what they express their faith through. The project talks about the religion itself. That's why the Quran verses are in Arabic calligraphy.
On why Islam was chosen at all:
I said: 
Elective doesn't fix it. 

I'm glad the Islam content is elective, but that doesn't resolve my concern it still scares me that it's offered at a Catholic school at all. And of all the religions to choose, why Islam? The girls could learn about Judaism or Christianity, the faiths that come from Catholicism's own roots. Why was Islam chosen over those?
They answered: That is how the Archdiocese-approved curriculum is designed, so all schools have the same curriculum.

text:
Charlie Strong estimates he interviewed for 20 head coaching jobs before he got one.

Lou Holtz coached his answers at South Carolina. Athletic director Mike McGee told him what the people conducting the interviews wanted to hear. The feedback never changed: poor interview, not prepared.

"I just feel like I'm a token," Strong told Holtz.

Holtz predicted the job would never come from an interview. Someone would call.

Years later, Louisville athletic director Tom Jurich arrived at Strong's house in Gainesville while he was outside playing kickball with his daughters. Strong, in shorts and a T-shirt, offered to change.

"No, no, no. I don't want you to change."

Twenty interviews taught Strong how to answer. One man drove to his house.

text:
The AM Brief, Friday November 13, 2026 Part 5

Happy Friday the 13th,

It’s 10am in Miami  and here is a recap of events in the Space sector that caught my eye. Part 5

     NASA has opened up to $10 billion in lunar cargo delivery contracts to eight private aerospace companies, including SpaceX and Blue Origin, to support the construction of a permanent south pole Moon Base by 2032. As part of this broader Artemis push, Blue Origin also secured a $94 million award to land a nuclear powered rover on the lunar surface in 2028. Simultaneously, the space agency is actively recruiting its next class of astronauts, offering a $164,395 salary with applications closing December 3.

     NASA's twin ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft have successfully executed a critical Earth gravity assist slingshot maneuver, putting the mission firmly on its interplanetary trajectory toward the Red Planet. The twin probes are scheduled to arrive at Mars in September 2027, where they will enter orbit to study how the solar wind interacts with the Martian magnetosphere and drives atmospheric escape over time.

     Defense contractor Kratos Defense has partnered with Seagate Space to establish a commercial offshore launch facility. The companies plan to deploy a mobile launch platform capable of sending orbital and suborbital rockets into space directly from maritime waters beginning in 2027. This sea based launch approach aims to bypass congested land based launch infrastructure, increase operational flexibility, and offer customizable launch trajectories for commercial and military satellite payloads.

     Astronomers using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile discovered 2026 ED138, a potential sixth dwarf planet in our solar system. The celestial object orbits far beyond Pluto at roughly 46 times the distance between Earth and the sun. Following the initial detection, researchers successfully confirmed its orbital trajectory by tracing its location backward through historical observational images dating back to 2016.

     Scientific analysis of the Saharan meteorite Teghaza 001 has confirmed it as one of the oldest physical fragments of Mars ever discovered on Earth. Geochemical dating places the rock's age at more than 4.1 billion years, offering researchers a rare direct sample of the Martian crust from the red planet's early geological epoch. The ancient meteorite provides planetary scientists with invaluable chemical clues regarding early planetary differentiation, crust formation, and environmental conditions present during the initial formation of the inner solar system's terrestrial worlds.

Sources : The Flyover (11-10), The Flyover (11-12), Mindstream (11-11), 1% Better (10-29), Superhuman (11-8)

Thank you for reading
Live your best life,
AL Maulini

🇺🇸 🇮🇱 | Gofman’s Washington–Miami Mission: Where Diplomacy and Military Deterrence Converge

Mossad Director Roman Gofman’s visit to the United States deserves attention not simply for the senior officials he is meeting, but for the sequence and strategic context of his engagements. His consultations in Washington, followed by an anticipated meeting in Miami with @SEPeaceMissions Steve Witkoff, point to a mission that operates at the intersection of intelligence, security coordination and high-level diplomacy.

The Miami meeting is particularly significant. Witkoff is central to President Donald Trump’s diplomatic channel with Tehran and plays a key role in the administration’s efforts to shape a possible negotiated outcome. Gofman’s anticipated discussions with him therefore suggest that Israel wants to engage directly with the American diplomatic process, communicate its strategic assessments and ensure that its security concerns are not sidelined in Washington’s calculations.

The timing is equally important. Reports that @CENTCOM has been advising Israeli military representatives and Gulf partners to prepare for the possibility of renewed hostilities against Iran sit uneasily alongside Trump’s public insistence that he sees no immediate need to resume military operations. Meanwhile, the continuing deployment of American military assets to the region suggests that Washington is maintaining a substantial capacity for escalation.

There is, however, no necessary contradiction between diplomatic engagement and military preparedness. The Trump administration may be seeking to preserve diplomatic options while ensuring that Tehran understands the military consequences of a breakdown in negotiations. Deterrence can serve diplomacy, just as diplomacy can provide an alternative to military confrontation.

Gofman’s mission should therefore be viewed against this broader strategic picture. Washington and Jerusalem have a shared interest in preventing Iran from emerging stronger from the current confrontation, but they may not necessarily have identical calculations about the timing, scope or desirability of renewed military action.

The central question is whether the United States is using military readiness to reinforce its negotiating position or preparing for the possibility that diplomacy will fail. The two objectives are not mutually exclusive. For now, Washington appears determined to keep both options open — and Gofman’s meetings may offer an important indication of how closely Israeli and American strategic thinking remains aligned.

“Nobody can guarantee results.” But you want me to guarantee your payment for the next six months.

Hyundai guaranteed the engine in every car it sold for 10 years. The average business owner won't guarantee their own work for 10 days.

Hyundai was a punchline when it made that promise.

In 1998 it sold about 90,000 cars in the U.S., the lowest number in its history. The man running its American business said later that they were deciding whether to stay in North America at all.

That fall Hyundai put a 10 year, 100,000 mile warranty on the engine and transmission of every new car.

People in the industry said it would come back to bite them.

Sales rose 82% the next year.

By 2002 they had passed 360,000.

The cars had improved too. The warranty is what made people believe it.

Hyundai did it again in 2009.

If you bought a car and lost your job within a year, you could hand it back.

The U.S. car market fell 21% that year. Hyundai's sales went up 8%.

Hampton Inn started telling guests in 1989 that if they weren't satisfied, they didn't pay.

Any employee could give the money back, whether they ran the hotel or cleaned the rooms.

People inside the company thought it would give the rooms away.

It tested the idea first. One hotel in Pennsylvania got 10 refund requests out of about 8,500 guests.

Over the first 10 years the chain gave away more than $6 million in free rooms.

It tracked more than $41 million in repeat business from the guarantee.

Almost seven to one.

A pest control company in Miami called "Bugs" Burger Bug Killers sold to hotels and restaurants.

Most of its competitors promised to get pests down to acceptable levels. It promised none.

No bill until every pest was gone.

If it failed, the client got a refund and the company paid the fines.

It charged up to 10 times what its competitors charged.

In 1986 it paid out $120,000 on $33 million in sales.

L.L.Bean sold its first 100 pairs of boots in 1912. Ninety came back defective. Leon Leonwood Bean refunded every one and fixed the boot. The guarantee became what the company was known for.

Every one of these companies did the math most business owners refuse to do.

Every sale has risk in it, because the work might not deliver. Somebody has to hold that risk.

With no guarantee, your customer holds all of it, and customers charge you for holding it. They ask for a discount, or they go quiet and you never hear why.

Take the risk yourself and you're the one who gets paid for it. That is where the 10 times came from.

Risk gets paid. The only choice you have is who collects.

A guarantee also makes failure your bill.

Hyundai agreed to pay for every bad engine for 10 years, so it had to build better engines. "Bugs" Burger trained every technician for six months, because a job that failed didn't get paid.

With no guarantee, the customer pays for your failed work, and nothing forces you to get better.

An agency that keeps the retainer when the work didn't deliver has put all of the risk on the customer.

If you sell marketing, SEO, or ads, you're being paid to make your client more money than they'd make without you. If you don't deliver that, you should give their money back.

Thinking you're getting paid for the activity is thinking like an employee.

A refund has a name on it. It leaves your bank account with a customer attached, and it stings.

The sale you lost because the buyer had to carry the risk has no name and never shows up on a report. So you count the first and never count the second.

It's worse in a service business. A car can be test driven. Nobody can test drive six months of SEO. The buyer is paying for a promise, so the risk they hold is as high as it gets.

That makes a guarantee more valuable in a service business than in any other kind. It's also where a guarantee is hardest to find.

And if promising a result makes your stomach drop, you already know something about your work that your customers don't.

So price it like anything else.

Start with what it costs. Hampton's own estimate is that about 1% of revenue goes to honoring the guarantee. "Bugs" Burger paid out about a third of 1%.

Then find out what it adds. Offer the guarantee on your next 20 sales calls and count how many more people say yes. Count the refunds as they come in.

It doesn't have to be unconditional. "Bugs" Burger made its clients keep the place clean as part of the deal. Put your terms in writing.

Some people will abuse it. L.L.Bean had customers returning items they'd picked up at yard sales. In 2018, after losing $250 million in five years on returns headed for the landfill, it put a one year limit on the guarantee. It kept the guarantee.

Stop counting the refunds you might give.

Start counting the sales you never got.

Think Big.

text:
The AM Brief, Friday November 13, 2026 Part 2

Happy Friday the 13th,

It’s 10am in Miami  and here is a recap of labor related events that caught my eye. Part 2

     Recent labor market data updates revealed notable upward revisions to late summer U.S. employment figures, signaling stronger underlying job growth than initially reported. The August payroll numbers were revised upward by 53,000 jobs, while September’s figures saw an upward adjustment of 31,000 positions. Combined, these revisions add 84,000 jobs to the two-month tally, offering economists and policymakers a slightly firmer picture of domestic labor resilience heading into year end.

     A broad PwC study surveying 49,364 workers across 48 countries highlights a growing disconnect in corporate technology adoption. While workplace artificial intelligence utilization increased significantly to reach 64%, access to necessary training programs simultaneously dropped from 59% to 51%. This widening capability gap suggests that while companies are pushing rapid operational integration of automated tools, they are failing to provide employees with sufficient educational resources and structured guidance to effectively navigate the shift.

      An increasing number of Generation Z Americans are opting out of traditional four year university degrees in favor of vocational trade schools, paid apprenticeships, and short term technical certification programs. Driven by soaring college tuition costs, student debt aversion, and strong wage growth in skilled trades, younger workers are gravitating toward hands on careers in construction, manufacturing, healthcare, and energy infrastructure that offer faster entry into the workforce.

     New demographic and labor data indicates that fathers are now nearly as likely as mothers to utilize state administered paid family leave programs across several U.S. states. The narrowing gender gap in leave claims reflects shifting workplace norms, broader cultural acceptance of paternal caregiving, and expanded state level statutory benefits that encourage both parents to take time off following the birth or adoption of a child.

Sources : Tangle Sunday Edition (11-8), MyClaw Newsletter (11-1), The Epoch Times Morning Brief (11-8), 1440 Sunday Edition (11-8)

Thank you for reading
Live your best life,
AL Maulini

text:
Sam Hartman is a practice squad quarterback for the Commanders, and he's now the next star of ABC's "The Bachelor." He landed the lead on TV before he got one in the NFL.

He's 27 and from Charlotte, and in college he was one of the most productive quarterbacks ever. At Wake Forest he set ACC records for career touchdown passes and 300-yard games, then played his last season at Notre Dame. All of that came after a scare in 2022, when he was diagnosed with Paget-Schroetter syndrome, a rare condition that causes blood clots in a vein near the collarbone. He returned the next year and won the ACC's Brian Piccolo Award for courage.

The pros haven't gone the same way. He went undrafted in 2024 and signed with Washington, and On3 counts eight roster moves since: waived, practice squad, elevated, released, back on the practice squad, a future contract, waived again and back on the practice squad. He still hasn't played a regular season snap. This preseason he went 25 for 46 for 207 yards and four picks before Washington cut him and brought him back to the practice squad.

That spot pays the minimum by NFL standards: $13,750 a week in 2026 for a player with two or fewer seasons, roughly $247,500 over 18 weeks, per Front Office Sports. Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota are both ahead of him.

"The Bachelor" might pay off better. ABC doesn't share salaries, but recent leads have reportedly gotten at least $100,000, TV Insider reported, citing Reality Steve. Jason Tartick has said he and Colton Underwood were each offered $100,000 for the role. Most of the money tends to come later, from sponsorships and brand deals once millions of people know your face.

He's not the first football player to do it. Colton Underwood, a practice squad journeyman himself, led Season 23 in 2019. Hartman told Good Morning America he's "excited but also very nervous," and said talking to one woman is hard enough, never mind 30.

Season 30 premieres March 21, 2027, on ABC.

text:
Porto Katsiki Beach in Lefkada

There are beaches that are lovely for a swim, and then there are places that make you stop and admire the scenery before you've even reached the water. Porto Katsiki, on the southwestern coast of Lefkada, belongs firmly in the second category.

The beach is famous for its towering white cliffs, pale shoreline and brilliant blue sea. From the viewpoint above, the contrast between the rock formations and the Ionian water creates one of the most impressive coastal panoramas in Greece.

A staircase leads down towards the beach, where the landscape feels even more dramatic. The cliffs provide a striking backdrop, while the water changes colour depending on the sunlight and sea conditions.

Here are some of the highlights of a visit:
•  Take in the view from above: Stop at the viewpoint before heading down to appreciate the full scale of the beach.
•  Swim in the Ionian Sea: Enjoy the clear water and striking shades of blue on a calm day.
•  Explore the shoreline: Walk along the beach and admire the impressive white cliffs surrounding it.
•  Bring your camera: The views from the top and the beach itself are among Lefkada's most memorable photo opportunities.
•  Enjoy the coastal scenery: The drive towards Porto Katsiki offers beautiful views of the island's western coastline.

Porto Katsiki is especially popular during the summer, so arriving early is a good idea if you want to enjoy a little more space. Facilities can be seasonal, and the beach is exposed to changing sea conditions, so check the weather before setting out.

The shoreline can be a mix of sand and pebbles, and the water may become deep quite close to the beach. Take care when swimming, particularly when there is a swell, and wear suitable footwear for the steps and beach surface.

Lefkada has several other spectacular beaches along its western coast, including Egremni and Kathisma, so you could easily make a day of exploring this part of the island.

But Porto Katsiki has a special quality of its own. With its dramatic cliffs, brilliant water and unforgettable setting, it is easy to understand why it has become one of Greece's most celebrated beaches.
